title.zh: 卷十二 志第二 歷上
title.raw: 卷十二 志第二 歷上 Volume 12 Treatises 2: Calendar 1

sentences.zh: 夫天地之所貴者生也，萬物之所尊者人也，役智窮神，無幽不察，是以動作云為，皆應天地之象。

translations.literal: That which Heaven and Earth hold precious is life; that which the myriad things hold in honor is humanity. Employing wisdom and exhausting the spirit, nothing in the hidden realms escapes scrutiny—therefore in movement and action, in speech and conduct, all correspond to the images of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Life is what Heaven and Earth prize most; among the myriad creatures, it is humanity that commands the highest regard. By applying intellect and pushing the mind to its limits, nothing concealed lies beyond notice; thus every deed and utterance answers to the patterns of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 古先聖哲，擬辰極，制渾儀。

translations.literal: The ancient sage worthies modeled the celestial pole and fashioned the armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: The sage rulers of antiquity took the celestial pole as their model and devised the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 夫陰陽二氣，陶育羣品，精象所寄，是為日月。

translations.literal: The two qi of yin and yang nurture the multitude of kinds; the refined images to which they attach are the sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang—the two vital breaths—shape and nourish all living kinds; the luminous bodies in which their essence is embodied are the sun and the moon.

sentences.zh: 羣生之性，章為五才，五才之靈，五星是也。

translations.literal: The nature of living multitudes is manifest as the five talents; the spirit of the five talents is the five stars.
translations.idiomatic: The character of all living things displays itself in the five endowments, and the animating power of those five endowments resides in the five planets.

sentences.zh: 曆所以擬天行而序七耀，紀萬國而授人時。

translations.literal: The calendar is that whereby one models the motion of Heaven and orders the seven luminaries, records the myriad states, and bestows the seasons upon humanity.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar exists to mirror the course of Heaven, set the seven luminaries in sequence, register the affairs of the myriad realms, and grant humankind its proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 黃帝使大撓造六甲，容成制曆象，羲和占日，常儀占月。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor had Da Rao create the six jia; Rong Cheng devised the calendar and celestial markers; Xi He observed the sun, Chang Yi observed the moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor charged Da Rao with devising the six jia cycle; Rong Cheng established the calendar and its celestial models; Xi He took charge of observing the sun, and Chang Yi of observing the moon.

sentences.zh: 少昊氏有鳳鳥之瑞，以鳥名官，而鳳鳥氏司曆。

translations.literal: In the age of Shaohao there was the auspice of the phoenix bird; he named his offices after birds, and the Phoenix Bird Office managed the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaohao the phoenix appeared as a favorable omen; he named his ministries after birds, and the Ministry of the Phoenix Bird oversaw the calendar.

sentences.zh: 顓頊之代，南正重司天，北正黎司地。

translations.literal: In the age of Zhuanxu, the southern rectifier Chong managed Heaven, and the northern rectifier Li managed Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhuanxu's time Chong, rectifier of the south, governed affairs of Heaven, while Li, rectifier of the north, governed affairs of Earth.

sentences.zh: 堯復育重黎之後，使治舊職，分命羲、和，欽若昊天。

translations.literal: Yao again nurtured the descendants of Chong and Li, had them administer their former duties, and separately charged Xi and He to revere the vast Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yao in turn raised up the line of Chong and Li, restored them to their former offices, and separately appointed Xi and He with the charge to honor the great Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故虞書曰：「朞三百有六旬六日，以閏月定四時成歲。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents of Yu says: "The full period is three hundred and sixty-six days and six parts of a day; intercalary months fix the four seasons and complete the year."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Yu section of the Documents states: "The full cycle is three hundred sixty-six days and a fractional sixth; intercalary months establish the four seasons and complete the year."

sentences.zh: 」其後授舜，曰：「天之曆數在爾躬。

translations.literal: Thereafter he handed it to Shun, saying: "The calendrical mandate of Heaven rests upon your person."
translations.idiomatic: He then passed the charge to Shun, saying, "Heaven's calendrical mandate is vested in you alone."

translations.literal: Shun likewise charged Yu with it.
translations.idiomatic: Shun in turn entrusted the same charge to Yu.

sentences.zh: 爰及殷、周二代，皆創業革制，而服色從之。

translations.literal: Down through the Yin and Zhou, both dynasties founded their rule and reformed their institutions, and ceremonial colors followed these changes.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Yin and Zhou dynasties alike, each new house founded its rule and revised its institutions, and court ritual colors followed suit.

sentences.zh: 順其時氣，以應天道，萬物羣生，蒙其利澤。

translations.literal: Complying with seasonal qi, they responded to the Way of Heaven; the myriad things and living multitudes received their benefit and grace.
translations.idiomatic: By aligning with the seasonal breaths they answered Heaven's Way, and the myriad creatures reaped the benefit of that harmony.

sentences.zh: 三王既謝，史職廢官，故孔子正春秋以明司曆之過。

translations.literal: After the Three Kings passed away, the historiographical offices were abolished and their posts fell vacant; therefore Confucius corrected the Spring and Autumn to expose the failings of the calendar officers.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Three Kings were gone, the historiographical service lapsed and its posts stood empty; for this reason Confucius rectified the Spring and Autumn to lay bare the errors of those charged with the calendar.

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，自以為水德，以十月為正，服色上黑。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm, it took itself to be of the Water phase, made the tenth month the first month of the year, and set ceremonial colors to black above all.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the empire, it claimed the Water phase as its own, took the tenth month as the year's beginning, and elevated black in ritual dress.

sentences.zh: 漢興，襲秦正朔，北平侯張蒼首言律曆之事，以顓頊曆比於六曆，所失差近。

translations.literal: When Han arose, it adopted Qin's calendar and new year's month; Marquis of Beiping Zhang Cang was first to speak on pitch-pipes and the calendar, comparing the Zhuanxu calendar with the six calendars—the errors were nearly the same.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han the dynasty retained Qin's calendar and new year's day; Zhang Cang, Marquis of Beiping, was the first to address matters of pitch-pipes and the calendar, comparing the Zhuanxu system with the six rival calendars—and the discrepancies proved almost equally slight.

sentences.zh: 施用至武帝元封七年，太中大夫公孫卿、壺遂、太史令司馬遷等，言曆紀廢壞，宜改正朔，易服色，所以明受之於天也。

translations.literal: It was employed until the seventh year of Emperor Wu's Yuanfeng era, when Grand Master of Palace Gongsun Qing, Hu Sui, Grand Astrologer Sima Qian, and others said the calendrical cycle had fallen into ruin and the new year's month and ceremonial colors ought to be changed, thereby making clear that mandate was received from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This system remained in use until the seventh year of Yuanfeng, when Gongsun Qing, Hu Sui, Sima Qian as Grand Astrologer, and others declared that the calendrical cycle had broken down and that the new year's month and ritual colors should be revised to show plainly that the mandate came from Heaven.

translations.literal: An edict then charged Sui and the others to create the Han calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accordingly ordered Sui and his colleagues to draft the Han calendar.

sentences.zh: 選鄧平、長樂司馬可及人間治曆者，二十餘人。

translations.literal: Deng Ping, the Director of Changle, Sima Ke, and more than twenty others skilled in calendrical matters among the populace were selected.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ping, Director of Changle, Sima Ke, and more than twenty calendar specialists drawn from the general population were chosen for the task.

sentences.zh: 方士唐都分天部，落下閎運算轉曆。

translations.literal: The fangshi Tang Du divided the celestial departments; Luoxia Hong calculated and turned the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The adept Tang Du apportioned the celestial regions, while Luoxia Hong performed the calculations that set the calendar in motion.

sentences.zh: 其法積八十一寸，則一日之分也。

translations.literal: The method accumulates eighty-one parts to make one day's fractional portion.
translations.idiomatic: By that method, eighty-one fractional parts accumulate to constitute one day's fractional share.

translations.literal: Hong and Ping treated the same material.
translations.idiomatic: Luoxia Hong and Deng Ping worked from the same principles.

sentences.zh: 於是皆觀星度，日月行，更以算推，如閎、平法，一月之日二十九日八十一分日之四十三。

translations.literal: Thereupon all observed the stars' positions and the sun and moon's motion, and by further calculation it matched Hong and Ping's method: a month's days were twenty-nine and forty-three eighty-firsts of a day.
translations.idiomatic: They then observed stellar positions and the courses of the sun and moon; further reckoning confirmed Hong and Ping's formula—a lunar month comprised twenty-nine days and forty-three eighty-firsts of a day.

sentences.zh: 詔遷用鄧平所造八十一分律曆，以平為太史丞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qian to employ the eighty-first-part pitch-pipe calendar that Ping had made, and Ping was made Assistant Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Sima Qian to adopt the eighty-first-part pitch-pipe calendar that Ping had devised, and Ping was appointed Assistant Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 至元鳳三年，太史令張壽王上書，以為元年用黃帝調曆，「今陰陽不調，更曆之過」。

translations.literal: By the third year of Yuanfeng, Grand Astrologer Zhang Shouwang submitted a memorial saying that in the inaugural year the Yellow Emperor's tuning calendar had been used: "Now yin and yang are not in harmony—it is the fault of changing the calendar."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng, Grand Astrologer Zhang Shouwang memorialized the throne, arguing that the inaugural year had employed the Yellow Emperor's tuning calendar: "Yin and yang are now out of harmony because the calendar was changed."

sentences.zh: 詔下主曆使者鮮于妄人與治曆大司農中丞麻光等二十餘人雜候晦朔弦望二十四氣。

translations.literal: An edict sent it down to the Chief Calendar Officer Xianyu Wangren, Director of Agriculture Assistant Director Ma Guang, and more than twenty others to observe together the new moon, full moon, first and third quarters, and the twenty-four qi.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Chief Calendar Officer Xianyu Wangren, Assistant Director of Agriculture Ma Guang, and more than twenty colleagues jointly to observe new moons, full moons, quarter moons, and the twenty-four seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 又詔丞相、御史、大將軍、右將軍史各一人雜候上林清臺，課諸疏密，凡十一家。

translations.literal: Another edict charged one man each from the offices of the Chancellor, Imperial Secretary, Grand Marshal, and Right General's clerical staff to observe jointly at the Clear Terrace in Shanglin, assessing each scheme's density or looseness—eleven houses in all.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict assigned one clerk each from the chancellor, imperial secretary, grand marshal, and right general to observe at the Clear Terrace in Shanglin and grade every system for tightness or slack—eleven schools in all.

translations.literal: They began in the third year and finished in the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Observations began in the third year and ran through the fifth.

translations.literal: Shouwang's system was graded loose and remote.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwang's calendar ranked lowest for being loose and far off the mark.

sentences.zh: 又漢元年不用黃帝調曆，劾壽王逆天地，[1]大不敬。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Han's inaugural year the Yellow Emperor's tuning calendar had not been used; Shouwang was impeached for opposing Heaven and Earth—a capital offense of supreme irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han's inaugural year had not in fact used the Yellow Emperor's tuning calendar; Shouwang was charged with defying Heaven and Earth—a grave offense of supreme irreverence.

translations.literal: An edict said not to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade proceeding with the impeachment.

sentences.zh: 復候，盡六年，太初曆第一。

translations.literal: Observations resumed until the sixth year; the Taichu calendar ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Observations were resumed through the sixth year, and the Taichu calendar placed first.

sentences.zh: 壽王曆乃太史官殷曆也。

translations.literal: Shouwang's calendar was in fact the Yin calendar kept by the Grand Astrologer's office.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwang's system turned out to be the Yin calendar preserved in the Grand Astrologer's archives.

translations.literal: Shouwang was impeached again and would not submit; in the end he was handed to the judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouwang was impeached a second time and refused to yield, he was at last remanded to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 至孝成時，劉向總六曆，列是非，作五紀論。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Cheng, Liu Xiang summarized the six calendars, arrayed right and wrong, and composed the Wuji lun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng, Liu Xiang surveyed the six calendars, weighed their merits and faults, and wrote the Treatise on the Five Cycles.

sentences.zh: 向子歆作三統曆以說春秋，屬辭比事，雖盡精巧，非其實也。

translations.literal: Xiang's son Xin made the Santong calendar to expound the Spring and Autumn; though its phrasing and parallels were exquisitely wrought, it did not match reality.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's son Xin devised the Triple Concordance calendar to interpret the Spring and Autumn; for all its ingenious phrasing and parallel structures, it did not accord with fact.

sentences.zh: 班固謂之密要，故漢曆志述之。

translations.literal: Ban Gu called it subtle and essential, and therefore the Han Treatise on the Calendar records it.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu pronounced it subtle and essential, which is why the Han Treatise on the Calendar preserves it.

sentences.zh: 校之何承天等六家之曆，雖六元不同，分章或異，至今所差，或三日，或二日數時，考其遠近，率皆六國及秦時人所造。

translations.literal: Compared with the calendars of He Tiancheng and five other houses, though their six origins differed and their fractional divisions varied, down to the present the discrepancies amount to three days, or two days and several hours; examining their antiquity, on the whole they were all made by men of the Six States and Qin times.
translations.idiomatic: Set against the calendars of He Tiancheng and five other schools—though their six origins differed and their fractional schemes diverged—the accumulated error down to the present runs to three days, or two days and several hours; judged by antiquity, nearly all were the work of scholars from the Six States and Qin.

sentences.zh: 其術斗分多，上不可檢於春秋，下不驗於漢、魏，雖復假稱帝王，祇足以惑時人耳。

translations.literal: Their methods have large dipper fractions and cannot be checked against the Spring and Autumn above or verified against Han and Wei below; even if they falsely claim imperial authorship, they suffice only to mislead their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Their methods employ oversized dipper fractions: they cannot be tested against the Spring and Autumn in earlier times nor confirmed against Han and Wei in later ones; even when they falsely attribute themselves to ancient emperors, they are fit only to delude the men of their own day.

sentences.zh: 光武建武八年，太僕朱浮上言曆紀不正，宜當改治。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Emperor Guangwu's Jianwu era, Grand Minister Zhu Fu memorialized that the calendrical cycle was incorrect and ought to be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jianwu under Emperor Guangwu, Grand Minister Zhu Fu submitted a memorial stating that the calendrical cycle was wrong and should be corrected.

translations.literal: The discrepancy at the time was still slight, and there was no leisure to examine and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: The error was still small, and the court had no leisure to undertake a full correction.

sentences.zh: 明帝永平中，待詔楊岑、張盛、景防等典治曆，但改易加時弦望，未能綜校曆元也。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era of Emperor Ming, awaiting-edict Yang Cen, Zhang Sheng, Jing Fang, and others managed the calendar but only altered the hours of addition for quarter moons—they could not comprehensively verify the calendar's origin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming in the Yongping period, Yang Cen, Zhang Sheng, Jing Fang, and other awaiting-edict scholars oversaw the calendar but merely adjusted the hours at which quarter moons were marked; they could not carry out a full verification of the calendrical origin.

sentences.zh: 至元和二年，太初失天益遠，宿度相覺浸多，候者皆知日宿差五度，冬至之日在斗二十一度，晦朔弦望，先天一日。

translations.literal: By the second year of Yuanhe, the Taichu calendar's divergence from Heaven grew ever farther; lodge degrees felt the increase by degrees; observers all knew the sun's lodge was off by five degrees, winter solstice fell in the twenty-first degree of Dipper, and new moon, full moon, and quarters ran one day ahead.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Yuanhe the Taichu system's drift from Heaven had grown pronounced; stellar lodge positions showed a steadily widening gap; every observer knew the sun's lodge was five degrees in error, winter solstice stood in Dipper 21, and new moons, full moons, and quarters appeared a day too early.

sentences.zh: 章帝召治曆編訢、李梵等綜校其狀。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang summoned the calendar compilers Bian Xin, Li Fan, and others to examine the situation comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang summoned the calendar experts Bian Xin, Li Fan, and others to conduct a comprehensive review.

sentences.zh: [2]遂下詔書稱：「春秋保乾圖曰：『三百年斗曆改憲。

translations.literal: An edict then declared: "The Spring and Autumn and the Baojian tu say: 'Every three hundred years the Dipper calendar must change its statute.'"
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict citing the Spring and Autumn and the Baojian tu: "Every three hundred years the Dipper calendar must revise its standard."

sentences.zh: 』史官用太初鄧平術，有餘分一，在三百年之域，行度轉差，浸以繆錯，琁璣不正，文象不稽。

translations.literal: The historiographical officers use the Taichu and Deng Ping method, which has a surplus fraction of one; within the three-hundred-year span its motion turns increasingly discrepant, gradually erring; the jade sight-tube is not correct and the celestial patterns are not aligned.
translations.idiomatic: The court astronomers still employ the Taichu method of Deng Ping, which retains a surplus fraction of one; over the three-hundred-year span its computed motion drifts ever further astray; the sighting tube no longer points true, and the celestial patterns fail to match.

sentences.zh: 冬至之日，日在斗二十一度，[3]先立春一日，則四分之立春日也。

translations.literal: On the day of winter solstice the sun stood in the twenty-first degree of Dipper—one day before the Establishment of Spring, which is the day of Establishment of Spring in the Quarter-Day calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On winter solstice the sun stood in Dipper 21—one day before Establishment of Spring, which in the Quarter-Day calendar is itself the day of Establishment of Spring.

sentences.zh: 而以折獄斷大刑，於氣已逆；

translations.literal: Yet to settle lawsuits and impose capital punishment when the seasonal qi had already turned contrary—
translations.idiomatic: Yet to settle lawsuits and pronounce capital sentences when the seasonal breath had already reversed course—

translations.literal: to employ the full moon for harmony and balance was likewise far off the mark.
translations.idiomatic: to take the full moon as the moment of evenhanded justice was equally wide of the mark.

sentences.zh: 今改行四分，以遵堯順孔，奉天之文，同心敬授，儻獲咸熙。

translations.literal: Now we change to practice the Quarter-Day method, to follow Yao, accord with Confucius, uphold Heaven's pattern, unite our hearts in reverent bestowal, and perhaps attain universal brightness.
translations.idiomatic: We now adopt the Quarter-Day system to follow Yao, accord with Confucius, uphold Heaven's pattern, and with one accord reverently grant the seasons—perhaps thereby attaining universal radiance.

translations.literal: Thereupon the Quarter-Day method was put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The Quarter-Day calendar was thereupon put into effect.

sentences.zh: 黃帝以來諸曆以為冬至在牽牛初者皆黜焉。

translations.literal: All calendars since the Yellow Emperor that placed winter solstice at the beginning of Ox were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Every calendar since the Yellow Emperor that had placed winter solstice at the start of the Ox constellation was set aside.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元十四年，待詔太史霍融上言：「官漏刻率九日增減一刻，不與天相應，或時差至二刻半，不如夏曆密。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Emperor He's Yongyuan era, awaiting-edict Grand Astrologer Huo Rong memorialized: "The official clepsydra on average adds or subtracts one mark every nine days, not corresponding to Heaven; at times the error reaches two and a half marks—it is not as precise as the Xia calendar."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yongyuan under Emperor He, Grand Astrologer Huo Rong, then an awaiting-edict, wrote: "The official water clock gains or loses one notch every nine days on average, failing to match Heaven; at times the discrepancy reaches two and a half notches—it is less exact than the Xia calendar."

sentences.zh: 」其年十一月甲寅，詔曰：「漏所以節時分，定昏明。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jia-yin of that year, an edict said: "The clepsydra is what regulates the hours and fixes dusk and dawn."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year, on the day jia-yin, an edict declared: "The clepsydra exists to regulate the hours and fix dusk and dawn."

sentences.zh: 昏明長短，起於日去極遠近，日道周圜，不可以計率分。

translations.literal: The length of dusk and dawn arises from the sun's distance from the pole; the sun's path is circular and cannot be divided by proportional reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The varying length of dusk and dawn stems from how far the sun stands from the pole; the sun's path is circular and cannot be apportioned by simple proportional calculation.

sentences.zh: 官漏九日增減一刻，違失其實，以晷景為刻，密近有驗。

translations.literal: The official clepsydra's adding or subtracting one mark every nine days loses the reality; taking the gnomon shadow for the mark is close and has verification.
translations.idiomatic: The official practice of adding or subtracting one notch every nine days misses the reality; deriving the notches from gnomon shadows is tighter and can be verified.

sentences.zh: 今下晷景漏刻四十八箭。

translations.literal: Now issue the gnomon clepsydra of forty-eight arrow-tubes.
translations.idiomatic: Let the gnomon-based clepsydra of forty-eight arrow-tubes be issued.

sentences.zh: 」其二十四氣日所在，并黃道去極、晷景、漏刻、昏明中星，並列載于續漢律曆志。

translations.literal: The sun's position on each of the twenty-four qi, together with the yellow path's distance from the pole, gnomon shadow, clepsydra marks, dusk and dawn, and culminating stars at midnight, are all listed in the Treatise on Pitch-pipes and the Calendar in the Continued Han History.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's lodge on each of the twenty-four qi, together with the yellow path's polar distance, gnomon shadow, clepsydra gradations, hours of dusk and dawn, and midnight culminating stars, are all tabulated in the Continued Han Treatise on Pitch-pipes and the Calendar.

sentences.zh: 安帝延光三年，[4]中謁者亶誦上書言當用甲寅元，河南梁豐云當復用太初。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor An's Yanguang era, Palace Attendant Xuan recited a memorial saying the jia-yin origin ought to be used; Liang Feng of Henan said the Taichu ought to be restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanguang under Emperor An, Palace Attendant Xuan recited a memorial arguing for the jia-yin origin, while Liang Feng of Henan urged a return to the Taichu system.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎張衡、周興皆審曆，數難誦、豐，或不能對，或云失誤。

translations.literal: Secretarial Gentleman Zhang Heng and Zhou Xing were both versed in the calendar; they repeatedly challenged Xuan and Feng by calculation, and some could not reply, or they said there were errors.
translations.idiomatic: Secretarial Gentlemen Zhang Heng and Zhou Xing were both expert calendarists; they repeatedly cross-examined Xuan and Feng by calculation, and sometimes the latter could not answer, or their figures were shown to be wrong.

sentences.zh: 衡等參案儀注，考往校今，以為九道法最密。

translations.literal: Heng and the others examined the ritual protocols and compared past with present, holding the Nine Paths method to be tightest.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and his colleagues reviewed the observatory regulations, compared past with present, and judged the Nine Paths method the most precise.

translations.literal: An edict sent the matter down to the excellencies and ministers for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the chief ministers for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 太尉愷等參議：「太初過天一度，月以晦見西方。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Kai and others deliberated jointly: "The Taichu overshoots Heaven by one degree; the moon appears in the west at the last day of the month."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Kai and others reported jointly: "The Taichu runs one degree ahead of Heaven, and the moon is seen in the west on the last day of the month."

sentences.zh: 元和改從四分，四分雖密於太初，復不正。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era it was changed to follow the Quarter-Day method; though the Quarter-Day is tighter than the Taichu, it is again not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanhe the court switched to the Quarter-Day system; although the Quarter-Day is tighter than the Taichu, it too is in error.

translations.literal: Neither can be used.
translations.idiomatic: Neither may be adopted.

sentences.zh: 甲寅元與天相應，合圖讖，可施行。

translations.literal: The jia-yin origin corresponds with Heaven and matches the charts and weft texts—it can be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The jia-yin origin accords with Heaven and agrees with the prognostic texts—it should be put into practice.

translations.literal: The debaters were not of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: The disputants could not agree.

sentences.zh: 尚書令忠上奏：「天之曆數，不可任疑從虛，以非易是。

translations.literal: Secretarial Director Zhong submitted: "Heaven's calendrical numbers cannot be entrusted to doubt and empty supposition, using the wrong to displace the right."
translations.idiomatic: Secretarial Director Zhong memorialized: "Heaven's calendrical numbers must not be left to doubt and groundless speculation, substituting error for truth."

translations.literal: Xuan and the others thereupon let the matter rest.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and his party accordingly let the proposal drop.

sentences.zh: 靈帝熹平四年，五官郎中馮光、沛相上計掾陳晃等言：「曆元不正，故盜賊為害。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Emperor Ling's Xiping era, Palace Gentleman Feng Guang and Chen Huang, reporting officer of Pei, said: "The calendrical origin is incorrect, and therefore bandits do harm."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiping under Emperor Ling, Palace Gentleman Feng Guang and Chen Huang, the Pei commandery reporting officer, declared: "The calendrical origin is wrong, and that is why robbers and rebels inflict harm."

sentences.zh: 曆當以甲寅為元，不用庚申，乞本庚申元經緯明文。

translations.literal: The calendar ought to take jia-yin as the origin and not use geng-shen; they begged the original texts of the classics and weft for the geng-shen origin.
translations.idiomatic: They argued that the calendar should adopt jia-yin as its origin rather than geng-shen, and requested the canonical and weft passages underlying the geng-shen origin.

sentences.zh: 」詔下三府，與儒林明道術者詳議。

translations.literal: An edict sent it to the Three Excellencies and to those among the Confucian forest who understood the Way and its techniques for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the question to the Three Excellencies and to Confucian scholars versed in the Way and its arts for thorough debate.

translations.literal: The ministers assembled for joint deliberation at the Minister of Education's offices.
translations.idiomatic: The officials gathered at the Minister of Education's headquarters to debate jointly.

sentences.zh: 議郎蔡邕曰：「曆數精微，術無常是。

translations.literal: Consulting Gentleman Cai Yong said: "Calendrical numbers are exquisitely subtle; in technique there is no constant right."
translations.idiomatic: Consulting Gentleman Cai Yong declared: "Calendrical reckoning is exquisitely subtle; no method remains permanently correct."

sentences.zh: 漢興承秦，曆用顓頊，元用乙卯。

translations.literal: When Han arose it inherited Qin; the calendar used was Zhuanxu's, and the origin used was yi-mao.
translations.idiomatic: At Han's founding the dynasty took over Qin's institutions; it employed the Zhuanxu calendar with the yi-mao origin.

sentences.zh: 百有二歲，孝武皇帝始改太初，元用丁丑。

translations.literal: After one hundred and two years Emperor Wu first changed to the Taichu, using the ding-chou origin.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred and two years later Emperor Wu first adopted the Taichu calendar, with the ding-chou origin.

sentences.zh: 行之百八十九歲，孝章帝改從四分，元用庚申。

translations.literal: It was practiced for one hundred eighty-nine years; Emperor Zhang changed to follow the Quarter-Day, using the geng-shen origin.
translations.idiomatic: That system remained in use for one hundred eighty-nine years until Emperor Zhang switched to the Quarter-Day calendar with the geng-shen origin.

sentences.zh: 今光等以庚申為非，甲寅為是。

translations.literal: Now Guang and the others hold geng-shen to be wrong and jia-yin to be right.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and his allies now declare geng-shen wrong and jia-yin correct.

sentences.zh: 按曆法，黃帝、顓頊、夏、殷、周、魯，各自有元。

translations.literal: According to calendrical method, the Yellow Emperor, Zhuanxu, Xia, Yin, Zhou, and Lu each had its own origin.
translations.idiomatic: By calendrical reckoning, the Yellow Emperor, Zhuanxu, Xia, Yin, Zhou, and Lu each possessed its own origin.

translations.literal: What Guang and Huang cite is the Yin calendar's origin.
translations.idiomatic: The origin that Guang and Huang invoke is that of the Yin calendar.

sentences.zh: 昔始用太初丁丑之後，六家紛錯，爭訟是非。

translations.literal: From the time the Taichu ding-chou was first used, six houses disputed in confusion, wrangling over right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: From the first adoption of the Taichu ding-chou origin, six rival schools quarreled without resolution, contesting right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 張壽王挾甲寅元以非漢曆，雜候清臺，課在下第。

translations.literal: Zhang Shouwang wielded the jia-yin origin against the Han calendar; mixed observations at the Clear Terrace placed him in the lowest rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shouwang had wielded the jia-yin origin against the Han calendar; joint observations at the Clear Terrace ranked his system last.

translations.literal: The Taichu's verification had no omissions or failures.
translations.idiomatic: The Taichu system's empirical tests showed no gaps or failures.

sentences.zh: 是則雖非圖讖之元，而有效於前者也。

translations.literal: Thus even though it was not the origin of the charts and weft texts, it had efficacy in earlier times.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, although it was not the origin favored by prognostic literature, it had proved effective in its own day.

sentences.zh: 及用四分以來，考之行度，密於太初，是又新元有效於今者也。

translations.literal: And from the use of the Quarter-Day onward, when motion was examined, it was tighter than the Taichu—this new origin again has efficacy in the present.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the Quarter-Day calendar came into use, examination of celestial motion has shown it tighter than the Taichu—the newer origin has again proved effective in our own time.

sentences.zh: 故延光中，亶誦亦非四分，言當用甲寅元，公卿參議，竟不施行。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Yanguang era Xuan's recitation also rejected the Quarter-Day, saying the jia-yin origin ought to be used; the excellencies and ministers deliberated jointly, yet in the end it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: That is why in the Yanguang period Xuan's memorial likewise rejected the Quarter-Day and urged the jia-yin origin—yet after joint deliberation by the chief ministers, the change was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 且三光之行，遲速進退，不必若一。

translations.literal: Moreover, the motion of the three luminaries—slow, swift, advancing, and retreating—is not necessarily uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the courses of the sun, moon, and planets—now slower, now swifter, advancing and retreating—need not be uniform.

translations.literal: Therefore there are ancient and modern methods.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there are methods suited to antiquity and methods suited to the present.

sentences.zh: 今術之不能上通於古，亦猶古術不能下通於今也。

translations.literal: Present methods cannot reach upward to antiquity, just as ancient methods cannot reach downward to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Methods of today cannot be extended upward to antiquity, just as ancient methods cannot be extended downward to the present.

sentences.zh: 又光、晃以考靈耀為本，二十八宿度數至日所在，錯異不可參校。

translations.literal: Moreover, Guang and Huang take the Kaoling yao as their basis; the degree numbers of the twenty-eight lodges to the sun's position show discrepancies that cannot be cross-checked.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, Guang and Huang treat the Kaoling yao as their authority, yet the lodge-degree figures for the sun's daily position contain irreconcilable discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 元和二年用至今九十二歲，而光、晃言陰陽不和，姦臣盜賊，皆元之咎。

translations.literal: From the second year of Yuanhe to the present is ninety-two years, yet Guang and Huang say yin and yang are not in harmony and treacherous ministers and bandits are all the fault of the origin.
translations.idiomatic: The Quarter-Day calendar adopted in Yuanhe 2 has been in use ninety-two years, yet Guang and Huang blame every disharmony of yin and yang and every traitor and thief on the calendrical origin.

sentences.zh: 元和詔書，文備義著，非羣臣議者所能變易。

translations.literal: The Yuanhe edict's text is complete and its meaning clear—it is not something that disputing ministers can alter.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanhe edict is complete in wording and firm in intent; it is not a matter that debating ministers may overturn.

sentences.zh: 」三公從邕議，以光、晃不敬，正鬼薪法。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies followed Yong's argument; Guang and Huang were deemed irreverent and sentenced under the ghost-labor statute.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies sided with Yong; Guang and Huang were judged irreverent and sentenced to convict labor under the ghost-labor statute.

translations.literal: An edict said not to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade imposing punishment.

sentences.zh: 何承天曰：夫曆數之術，若心所不達，雖復通人前識，無救其為敝也。

translations.literal: He Tiancheng said: The art of calendrical numbers—if the mind does not grasp it, even passing it before the keen sight of others cannot save it from defect.
translations.idiomatic: He Tiancheng remarked: In the art of calendrical reckoning, when the mind fails to comprehend the method, even the keenest experts cannot keep the system from breaking down.

sentences.zh: 是以多歷年歲，未能有定。

translations.literal: Therefore over many years and generations no fixity has been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, across many years and generations, no lasting standard has been settled.

sentences.zh: 四分於天，出三百年而盈一日。

translations.literal: The Quarter-Day relative to Heaven yields one surplus day in three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against Heaven, the Quarter-Day calendar accumulates one full day's error every three hundred years.

sentences.zh: 積代不悟，徒云建曆之本，必先立元，假言讖緯，遂關治亂，此之為蔽，亦已甚矣。

translations.literal: Generation after generation did not perceive it, vainly saying that to establish the root of a calendar one must first set an origin, falsely invoking charts and weft texts and thereby linking it to order and disorder—this delusion is already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Age after age failed to notice the drift, insisting that every new calendar must begin by fixing an origin, invoking prognostic texts to tie calendrical choice to the rise and fall of states—a delusion already carried to extremes.

sentences.zh: 劉歆三統法尤復疏闊，方於四分，六千餘年又益一日。

translations.literal: Liu Xin's Triple Concordance method is especially loose and wide; compared with the Quarter-Day, in six thousand-odd years it again adds one day.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin's Triple Concordance system is especially loose; set beside the Quarter-Day, it accumulates yet another day's error every six thousand years or so.

sentences.zh: 揚雄心惑其說，采為太玄，班固謂之最密，著于漢志；

translations.literal: Yang Xiong's mind was confused by the doctrine; he adopted it in the Taixuan, Ban Gu called it the tightest, and recorded it in the Han Treatises;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong was beguiled by the system and wove it into his Taixuan; Ban Gu pronounced it the most exact and entered it in the Han Treatises.

sentences.zh: 司彪因曰「自太初元年始用三統曆，施行百有餘年。

translations.literal: Sima Biao accordingly said, "From the first year of Taichu the Triple Concordance calendar began to be used, practiced for more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao then wrote, "The Triple Concordance calendar came into use in Taichu 1 and remained in force for more than a century.

sentences.zh: 」曾不憶劉歆之生，不逮太初，二三君子言曆，幾乎不知而妄言歟。

translations.literal: " Yet he did not recall that Liu Xin's birth did not reach Taichu—can it be that these two or three gentlemen speaking of the calendar almost spoke in ignorance?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he forgot that Liu Xin was born only after the Taichu reform—were these worthies, one wonders, debating the calendar in near-total ignorance?

sentences.zh: 光和中，穀城門候劉洪始悟四分於天疏闊，更以五百八十九為紀法，百四十五為斗分，造乾象法，又制遲疾曆以步月行。

translations.literal: In the Guanghe era, Liu Hong, gate warden of Gucheng, first realized the Quarter-Day was loose relative to Heaven; he changed to 589 as the era divisor and 145 as the dipper fraction, made the Qianxiang method, and also devised a slow-fast calendar to step the moon's motion.
translations.idiomatic: During Guanghe, Liu Hong of Gucheng Gate first saw that the Quarter-Day calendar no longer hugged the sky; he reset the era divisor to 589 and the dipper fraction to 145, created the Qianxiang system, and added a slow-fast lunar ephemeris.

sentences.zh: 方於太初、四分，轉精微矣。

translations.literal: Compared with Taichu and the Quarter-Day, it became progressively more precise.
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the Taichu and Quarter-Day systems, it marked a clear advance in precision.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初中，太史丞韓翊以為乾象減斗分太過，後當先天，造黃初曆，以四千八百八十三為紀法，一千二百五為斗分。

translations.literal: In Wei Emperor Wen's Huangchu period, Assistant Grand Astrologer Han Yi thought the Qianxiang had reduced the dipper fraction too much and would later anticipate heaven; he made the Huangchu calendar, taking 4883 as the era divisor and 1250 as the dipper fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wei Wendi's Huangchu reign, Deputy Astrologer Han Yi argued that Qianxiang had pared the dipper fraction too sharply and would eventually run ahead of the sky; he therefore drafted the Huangchu calendar with an era divisor of 4883 and a dipper fraction of 1250.

sentences.zh: 其後尚書令陳羣奏，以為「曆數難明，前代通儒多共紛爭。

translations.literal: Afterward Minister of Works Chen Qun memorialized, saying, "Calendrical reckoning is hard to clarify; learned scholars of former ages often disputed it together.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Chen Qun then submitted a memorial: "Calendar theory is notoriously opaque, and fine scholars of past dynasties rarely agreed."

sentences.zh: 黃初之元，以四分曆久遠疏闊，大魏受命，宜正曆明時。

translations.literal: At the Huangchu origin, because the Quarter-Day calendar had long been loose, Great Wei received the mandate and ought to reform the calendar and clarify the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangchu reform began from the premise that the old Quarter Remainder had grown hopelessly slack; now that Wei held the mandate, the seasons needed a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 韓翊首建黃初，猶恐不審，故以乾象互相參校。

translations.literal: Han Yi first proposed the Huangchu; still fearing it was not verified, he therefore had Qianxiang mutually cross-checked.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yi opened the discussion, yet his work still lacked rigorous vetting, so the Qianxiang system was brought in for a side-by-side test.

sentences.zh: 歷三年，更相是非，舍本即末，爭長短而疑尺丈，竟無時而決。

translations.literal: Over three years they alternately judged right and wrong, abandoning root for branch, arguing over lengths and doubting feet and yards—ultimately there was no time when it was decided.
translations.idiomatic: For three years the rival camps traded contradictory verdicts, quibbling over minutiae while missing the main issue, disputing measurements without end—and never reached a settlement.

sentences.zh: 按三公議，皆綜盡曲理，殊塗同歸，欲使效之璿璣，各盡其法，一年之間，得失足定，合於事宜。

translations.literal: According to the Three Excellencies' deliberations, all comprehensively exhaust subtle principle; different paths have the same return; they wished to have them tested on the armillary sphere, each exhausting its method; within one year gain and loss would be sufficient to determine—it accorded with the matter's requirements.
translations.idiomatic: The three high ministers replied that every proposal drew on solid classical principle and aimed at the same end by different routes; the thing to do was to run each system on the armillary instrument for a full year—then success and failure would show plainly, which fit the practical need.

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，尚書郎楊偉制景初曆，施用至于晉、宋。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time, Gentleman of the Secretariat Yang Wei made the Jingchu calendar; it was practiced down to Jin and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming, Secretariat official Yang Wei produced the Jingchu calendar, which remained in use through Jin and Song.

sentences.zh: 古之為曆者，鄧平能修舊制新，劉洪始減四分，又定月行遲疾，楊偉斟酌兩端，以立多少之衷，因朔積分設差，以推合朔月蝕。

translations.literal: Among the ancients who made calendars: Deng Ping could repair the old and innovate; Liu Hong first reduced the quarter fraction and also fixed the moon's slow and fast motion; Yang Wei weighed both extremes to establish the balanced middle, and on the basis of accumulated new-moon points set corrections to deduce conjunction and lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The great calendar makers of old each advanced the art in a different way: Deng Ping renewed inherited practice; Liu Hong first trimmed the quarter-day excess and modeled the moon's variable speed; Yang Wei split the difference between rival systems, then built correction tables from accumulated conjunction data to predict new moons and eclipses.

translations.literal: These three men were the skilled calendar makers of Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: These three were the foremost calendrical experts of Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 然而洪之遲疾，不可以檢春秋，偉之五星，大乖於後代，斯則洪用心尚疏，偉拘於同出上元壬辰故也。

translations.literal: Yet Hong's slow-fast system cannot be checked against the Spring and Autumn; Wei's five planets greatly deviate in later ages—this is because Hong's intent was still loose, and Wei was constrained by sharing the same upper origin of renchen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Hong's lunar tables fail when tested against the Spring and Autumn, and Yang Wei's planetary positions drift badly in later times—Hong's approach was still insufficiently rigorous, and Wei was hamstrung by forcing every calculation back to the shared renchen upper origin.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初元年，改定曆數，以建丑之月為正，改其年三月為孟夏四月。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu of Wei Emperor Ming, the calendrical numbers were changed and fixed; the month established in chou was taken as correct, and that year's third month was changed to early summer, the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 1 under Wei Emperor Ming the court reset the calendar: the chou month became month one, and what had been the third month was relabeled early summer, the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 其孟仲季月，雖與正歲不同，至於郊祀、迎氣，祭祠、烝嘗，巡狩、蒐田，分至啟閉，班宣時令，皆以建寅為正。

translations.literal: Although its first, second, and third months of the season differed from the standard year, as for suburban sacrifice, welcoming the qi, sacrificial offerings, autumn and spring feasts, imperial tours, hunts, the equinoxes and solstices and the opening and closing of the seasons, promulgating and proclaiming seasonal orders—all took the month established in yin as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal names no longer matched the Xia calendar, yet for suburban rites, qi-welcoming ceremonies, temple offerings, seasonal sacrifices, royal tours and hunts, the four turning points of the year, and the publication of seasonal edicts, the yin month still counted as the true pivot of the year.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，帝崩，復用夏正。

translations.literal: In the third year, first month, the emperor died; they again used the Xia standard month.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died in the first month of the third year, the court reverted to the Xia-style first month.

sentences.zh: 楊偉表曰：「臣攬載籍，斷考曆數，時以紀農，月以紀事，其所由來，遐而尚矣。

translations.literal: Yang Wei presented a memorial saying: "Your servant has perused the records, reckoned and examined calendrical numbers: the seasons are used to mark the farming year, the months to mark affairs; how this practice arose lies far in antiquity and has long been honored.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei wrote: "I have combed the sources and worked through the calendar's numbers: seasons organize agriculture, months organize administration—and that arrangement goes back to remote antiquity."

sentences.zh: 乃自少昊，則玄鳥司分，顓頊帝嚳，則重、黎司天，唐帝、虞舜則羲、和掌日。

translations.literal: From Shaohao onward, the Dark Bird presided over the equinoxes; Zhuanxu and Di Ku had Chong and Li regulate Heaven; the Tang Emperor and Shun of Yu had Xi and He manage the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Already under Shaohao the swallow asterism marked the equinoxes; under Zhuanxu and Di Ku, Chong and Li were charged with celestial regulation; under Yao and Shun, Xi and He took charge of the solar calendar.

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties continued this, so each age had sun officers.
translations.idiomatic: The three early dynasties kept the office, so every reign maintained specialists charged with the calendar.

sentences.zh: 日官司曆，則頒之諸侯，諸侯受之，則頒于境內。

translations.literal: The sun officers managed the calendar, then promulgated it to the feudal lords; the lords received it and promulgated it within their domains.
translations.idiomatic: Those officers set the calendar and issued it to the regional lords, who in turn published it inside their own territories.

sentences.zh: 夏后之代，羲、和湎淫，廢時亂日，則書載胤征。

translations.literal: In the age after Xia, Xi and He sank into debauchery, neglected the seasons and threw the days into confusion, so the Documents records the Punitive Expedition of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Later in the Xia era, Xi and He neglected their duty and deranged the calendar, which is why the Book of Documents preserves the punitive campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，審農時而重人事者，歷代然也。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, scrutinizing the farming seasons and taking human affairs seriously has been the constant practice of successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that every dynasty has treated careful timing for agriculture and attention to civic order as a standing principle.

sentences.zh: 逮至周室既衰，戰國橫騖，告朔之羊，廢而不紹，登臺之禮，滅而不遵。

translations.literal: When it came to the decline of the Zhou house, the Warring States ran rampant: the sheep for the first-day-of-month announcement was abandoned and not renewed; the observatory rites perished and were not observed.
translations.idiomatic: By late Zhou the realm fractured: monthly temple announcements lapsed, and observatory ceremonies died out.

sentences.zh: 閏分乖次而不識，孟陬失紀而莫悟，大火猶西流，而怪蟄蟲之不藏也。

translations.literal: Intercalary divisions fell out of sequence and went unrecognized; the first month lost its reckoning and no one corrected it; the Great Fire still streamed westward, yet people wondered that hibernating insects did not hide away.
translations.idiomatic: Leap months drifted out of place, the civil year's first month wandered, and while Antares still hung in the western sky, courtiers marveled at insects that failed to burrow—blind to the calendar's chaos.

sentences.zh: 是時也，天子不協時，司曆不書日，諸侯不受職，日御不分朔，人事不恤，廢棄農時。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven did not harmonize the seasons, the calendar officers did not record the days, the feudal lords did not accept their duties, the day-keepers did not fix new-moon days, human affairs went untended, and the farming seasons were cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: The king no longer coordinated the seasons, official scribes stopped reliably dating events, regional rulers ignored their responsibilities, astronomers lost track of true conjunctions, and governance neglected both people and the agricultural timetable.

sentences.zh: 仲尼之撥亂於春秋，託褒貶糾正，司曆失閏，則譏而書之，登臺頒朔，則謂之有禮。

translations.literal: Confucius, in setting right disorder through the Spring and Autumn Annals, relied on praise and blame to correct matters: when calendar officers missed intercalations he ridiculed and recorded it; when they ascended the observatory to issue the new-moon calendar he called that observance of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius used the Spring and Autumn to restore order through moral judgment: he mocked missed intercalations, yet praised rulers who climbed the terrace to proclaim the civil calendar as behaving ritually.

sentences.zh: 自此以降，暨于秦、漢，乃復以孟冬為歲首，閏為後九月，中節乖錯，時月紕繆，加時後天，蝕不在朔，累載相襲，[5]久而不革也。

translations.literal: From this downward to Qin and Han, they again took the tenth winter month as year-beginning, placed intercalary months after the ninth month, so mid-term solar nodes and civil months went awry; the added hours lagged behind Heaven; eclipses no longer fell on new-moon days; age after age inherited the error, [5] and long delayed reform.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Qin and Han the year again began in early winter, leap months were tacked after the ninth month, solar terms and lunar months slipped badly out of alignment, ephemeris corrections ran behind the sky, eclipses missed conjunction, and the mistake persisted reign after reign [5] without overhaul.

sentences.zh: 至武帝元封七年，始乃寤其繆焉。

translations.literal: It was not until the seventh year of Yuanfeng of Emperor Wu that the error was grasped.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Yuanfeng 7 did Emperor Wu recognize the fault.

sentences.zh: 於是改正朔，更曆數，使大才通人，造太初曆，校中朔所差，以正閏分，課中星得度，以考疏密，以建寅之月為正朔，以黃鍾之月為曆初。

translations.literal: Thereupon the beginning of the year was corrected, calendrical numbers were changed, great talents and learned men were ordered to make the Taichu calendar; the discrepancy at mid-conjunction was checked to fix the intercalary fraction, mid-heaven stars were verified for angular position to test tightness or looseness, the month with jianyin was taken as standard new year, and the month of the yellow-bell pitch-pipe as calendrical origin.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the civil calendar, commissioned the Taichu system, adjusted the leap fraction against true conjunctions, checked stellar longitudes, adopted jianyin as the first month of the year, and anchored the epoch in the yellow-bell month.

sentences.zh: 其曆斗分太多，後遂疏闊。

translations.literal: That calendar's dipper fraction was too large, and in later times it became coarse and loose.
translations.idiomatic: The Taichu system's fractional remainder for the Dipper was too big, so in later reigns it grew increasingly imprecise.

sentences.zh: 至元和二年，復用四分曆，施而行之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe they reverted to the Quarter-Day calendar and applied it in practice.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanhe 2 the Quarter-Day calendar returned and was put back into use.

sentences.zh: 至于今日，考察日蝕，率常在晦，是則斗分太多，故先密後疏而不可用也。

translations.literal: Down to the present, examining solar eclipses, they almost always occur on the last day of the month—thus the dipper fraction was too large, so it was first tight and later loose and unusable.
translations.idiomatic: Eclipse records down to our own day show conjunctions drifting to month-end—proof the fractional excess was too large, yielding an apparently tight fit that soon loosened into uselessness.

sentences.zh: 是以臣前以制典餘日，推考天路，稽之前典，驗之食朔，詳而精之，更建密歷，則不先不後，古今中天。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant, using the surplus days of the statutory canon, traced the celestial track, collated earlier classics, tested with eclipse and conjunction data, refined it in detail, and established a tighter calendar so that neither early nor late it stands midway between ancient and modern mid-heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I reworked the official surplus-day reckoning, checked it against eclipses and prior canons, and drew up a denser calendar that tracks the sky evenly—neither ahead nor behind—between antiquity and today.

sentences.zh: 以昔在唐帝，協日正時，允釐百工，咸熙庶績也。

translations.literal: Thus in antiquity under Emperor Yao the days were harmonized and the seasons rectified, so the hundred crafts were duly assigned and the myriad tasks flourished.
translations.idiomatic: This matches Yao's age, when aligning the days and seasons allowed every office to function and every undertaking to thrive.

sentences.zh: 欲使當今國之典禮，凡百制度，皆韜合往古，郁然備足，乃改正朔，更曆數，以大呂之月為歲首，以建子之月為曆初。

translations.literal: He desires that the state's canonical rites and the hundred institutions should all fold together with antiquity and stand complete; therefore he corrects the beginning of the year, changes calendrical numbers, takes the month of the great lü as year-head, and the month with jianzi as calendrical origin.
translations.idiomatic: He wants current state ritual and every institution to echo ancient models; so he resets the civil year, revises the calendrical constants, begins the year in the great-lü month, and sets the computational epoch in the jianzi month.

sentences.zh: 臣以為昔在帝代，則法曰顓頊，曩自軒轅，則曆曰黃帝。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that in the age of the emperors the method was called Zhuanxu; from the Yellow Emperor onward the calendar was called Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I note that each great reform named its system—the Zhuanxu method in the age of the emperors, the Yellow Emperor's calendar from Xuanyuan onward.

sentences.zh: 暨至漢之孝武，革正朔，更曆數，改元曰太初，因名太初曆。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Xiaowu of Han, who corrected the beginning of the year, changed calendrical numbers, and altered the reign title to Taichu, whence it was named the Taichu calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Han Emperor Wu likewise reformed the new year, revised the constants, and took the era name Taichu—giving the system its title.

sentences.zh: 今改元為景初，宜曰景初曆。

translations.literal: Now that the era name is changed to Jingchu, it should be titled the Jingchu calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reign era is now Jingchu, the new system ought to be called the Jingchu calendar.

sentences.zh: 臣之所建景初曆，法數則約要，施用則近密，治之則省功，學之則易知。

translations.literal: As for the Jingchu calendar your servant has devised, its constants are concise, in use it is close and dense, to administer it saves labor, and to study it is easy to understand.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingchu scheme I propose keeps the parameters lean yet numerically tight, runs efficiently in practice, and is straightforward to learn.

sentences.zh: 雖復使研桑心算，隸首運籌，重、黎司晷，羲、和察景，以考天路，步驗日月，究極精微，盡術數之極者，皆未如臣如此之妙也。

translations.literal: Even if one employed Yanzi's merchant reckoning, Lishou's counting rods, Chong and Li on the gnomon, Xi and He observing shadows, to investigate the celestial road, pace and verify sun and moon, exhaust the utmost fineness and reach the limit of computation, none could match the subtlety your servant has attained.
translations.idiomatic: No amount of legendary arithmetical skill—merchant Yan's mental sums, Lishou's rods, Chong and Li at the sundial, Xi and He at the solstice shadow—could match the precision I have reached.

sentences.zh: 是以累代曆數，皆疏而不密，自黃帝以來，改革不已。

translations.literal: Therefore the calendrical numbers of successive ages have all been loose rather than tight; from the Yellow Emperor onward they have been repeatedly reformed without end.
translations.idiomatic: That is why earlier dynasties' calendars always erred on the loose side, and why reform has followed reform ever since the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰元以來，至景初元年丁巳，歲積四千四十六，算上。

translations.literal: From the renchen origin down to the first year of Jingchu, the dingsi year, the accumulated count is 4046, counted on the stem.

translations.literal: This origin takes the celestial-standard month with jianzi and the yellow-bell month as calendrical beginning; in the year of the origin's head, at midnight on jiazi new moon and winter solstice coincide.
translations.idiomatic: The epoch uses the true winter month (jianzi) aligned with the yellow-bell pitch month as calendar zero, so at the origin year's start a Jiazi day begins at midnight exactly at winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求其數之所生者，置一紀積月以通數乘之，會通去之，所去之餘，紀差之數也。

translations.literal: To seek how this number is produced: set one era's accumulated months, multiply by the communication number, remove multiples of the conjunction communication; the remainder removed is the era-difference number.
translations.idiomatic: To derive it: take the months in one era, multiply by the communication number, discard full multiples of the conjunction communication constant; what remains defines the era increment.

sentences.zh: 以之轉加前紀，則得後紀。

translations.literal: By rotating and adding it to the preceding era, one obtains the following era.
translations.idiomatic: Add that increment to the previous era's rate to get the next era's rate.

sentences.zh: 加之未滿會通者，則紀首之歲天正合朔，月在日道裏。

translations.literal: If the addition does not fill the conjunction communication, then in the head year of the era the civil new year's conjunction has the moon on the inner side of the solar path.
translations.idiomatic: If the sum stays below the conjunction communication constant, the new moon at the era's first civil year lies inside the solar track.

translations.literal: If it fills and is removed, then the moon is on the outer side of the solar path.
translations.idiomatic: If it crosses and you subtract the product, the moon at conjunction lies outside the solar track.

sentences.zh: 加表滿在裏，加裏滿在表。

translations.literal: Add outer: when full it is inner; add inner: when full it is outer.
translations.idiomatic: Stepping from outside, a full increment places the moon inside; stepping from inside, a full increment places it outside.

sentences.zh: 遲疾紀差，三萬一百八十。

sentences.zh: 求其數之所生者，置一紀積月，以通數乘之，通周去之，餘以減通周，所減之餘，紀差之數也。

translations.literal: To seek how this number is produced: set one era's accumulated months, multiply by the communication number, remove multiples of the communication circuit constant; subtract the remainder from the communication circuit constant; the remainder subtracted is the era-difference number.
translations.idiomatic: To derive it: multiply one era's months by the communication number, reduce modulo the communication circuit constant, subtract the remainder from that constant; what is left is the era increment.

sentences.zh: 以之轉減前紀，則得後紀。

translations.literal: By rotating and subtracting it from the preceding era, one obtains the following era.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract that decrement from the prior era's anomaly rate to obtain the next.

translations.literal: If subtraction is insufficient, add the communication circuit constant.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot subtract, add the communication circuit constant first.

sentences.zh: 求次元紀差率，轉減前元甲寅紀差率，餘則次元甲子紀差率也。

translations.literal: To seek the next-origin era difference rate, rotate-subtract the prior-origin Jiayin era difference rate; the remainder is the next-origin Jiazi era difference rate.
translations.idiomatic: For the next grand origin, subtract the previous Jiayin-era rate from the Jiazi-era rate as prescribed to get the new Jiazi increment.

translations.literal: To seek the next era, use the method above.
translations.idiomatic: To advance to the following era, repeat the same rule.

sentences.zh: 推朔積月術曰：置壬辰元以來，盡所求年，外所求，以紀法除之，所得算外，所入紀第也，餘則入紀年數。

translations.literal: Method for pushing accumulated months from new moons: set from the Renchen origin through the year sought, excluding the year sought, divide by the era divisor; the obtained count outside the reckoning is which era one has entered; the remainder is the years entered within the era.
translations.idiomatic: To count lunations from the Renchen epoch up to but not including the target year, divide by 1,843: the quotient plus one gives the era index, the remainder the year within that era.

sentences.zh: 年以章月乘之，如章歲而一為積月，不盡為閏餘。

translations.literal: Multiply the years by rule months and divide by rule years for one accumulated month; what does not exhaust is the intercalary remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply that year-count by 235 and divide by 19 for total months; the remainder is the leap fraction.

sentences.zh: 閏餘十二以上，其年有閏。

translations.literal: If the intercalary remainder is twelve or more, that year has an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: A leap year occurs when the intercalary remainder reaches twelve or higher.

translations.literal: An intercalary month is determined by having no mid-climate in the month.
translations.idiomatic: The leap month is the lunar month that contains no major solar term.

sentences.zh: 推朔術曰：以通數乘積月，為朔積分，如日法而一為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing new moons: multiply accumulated months by the communication number to obtain the accumulated new-moon fraction; divide by the day divisor for one accumulated day; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To compute conjunction instants, multiply accumulated months by 134,630; divide by 4,559 for whole days; the residue is the fractional day.

sentences.zh: 以六十去積日，餘為大餘。

translations.literal: Remove sixty from accumulated days; the remainder is the large remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the day count modulo sixty for the sexagenary stem-branch index.

sentences.zh: 大餘命以紀，算外，所求年天正十一月朔日也。

translations.literal: Count the large remainder by the era, outside the reckoning: this is the new-moon day of the eleventh civil month of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: Index that remainder against the sexagenary cycle to name the day of the eleventh month's conjunction in the target civil year.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加大餘二十九，小餘二千四百一十九，小餘滿日法從大餘，命如前，次月朔日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add to the large remainder twenty-nine, to the small remainder two thousand four hundred nineteen; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the large remainder; count as before: this is the next month's conjunction day.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 29 to the day count and 2,419 to the fraction, carrying overflows by 4,559 into the day count, then read off the next conjunction.

sentences.zh: 小餘二千一百四十以上，其月大也。

translations.literal: If the small remainder is two thousand one hundred forty or more, that month is long.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional part is 2,140 or greater, the month is a long thirty-day month.

sentences.zh: 推弦望，加朔大餘七，小餘千七百四十四，小分一，小分滿二從小餘，小餘滿日法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，餘命以紀，算外，上弦日也。

translations.literal: To push first and third quarters and full moons: add to the new-moon large remainder seven, to the small remainder one thousand seven hundred forty-four, and to the minute fraction one; when the minute fraction fills two, carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the large remainder; when the large remainder fills sixty, remove it; count the remainder by the era, outside the reckoning: this is the first-quarter day.
translations.idiomatic: For quarters: add 7 days, 1,744 parts, and one small part to the new-moon line, propagating carries through the small-part, fractional-day, and sexagenary levels; the result names the first-quarter day.

translations.literal: Again adding, one obtains full moon, last quarter, and the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same addition chain to reach full moon, third quarter, and the next conjunction.

sentences.zh: 其月蝕望者，定小餘，如所近中節間限，限數以下者，[9]算上為日。

translations.literal: For months in which there is a lunar eclipse at full moon, fix the small remainder; if it falls like the gap limit of the nearest mid-term node, and is at or below the limit number, see note [9]: count upward for the day.
translations.idiomatic: When a lunar eclipse falls on the full moon, adjust the fractional day by the gap limit of the nearest major term; if the value lies at or under the limit number, per note [9], round upward to fix the day.

sentences.zh: 望在中節前後各四日以還者，視限數；

translations.literal: If full moon falls within four days on either side of the mid-term node, consult the limit number.
translations.idiomatic: When full moon lies within four days before or after the major term, use the standard limit figure.

sentences.zh: 望在中節前後各五日以上者，視間限。

translations.literal: If full moon falls five or more days before or after the mid-term node, consult the gap limit.
translations.idiomatic: When full moon sits five or more days away from the major term, switch to the wider gap-limit criterion instead.

sentences.zh: 推二十四氣術曰：置所入紀年，外所求，以餘數乘之，滿紀法為大餘，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for computing the twenty-four qi: set the years entered in the era, excluding the year sought, multiply by the remainder number; what fills the era divisor becomes the large remainder, what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To place the twenty-four solar terms: take years elapsed within the current era, not counting the target year, multiply by 9,670, divide by 1,843 for the day count, and keep the fractional remainder.

sentences.zh: 大餘滿六十去之，餘命以紀，算外，天正十一月冬至日也。

translations.literal: Remove sixty from the large remainder; count the remainder by the era, outside the reckoning: this is the winter-solstice day of the eleventh civil month of the celestial-standard year.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the day line modulo sixty and read it against the sexagenary cycle to name the winter solstice of the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 求次氣，加大餘十五，小餘四百二，小分十一，小分滿氣法從小餘，小餘滿紀法從大餘，[10]命如前，次氣日也。

translations.literal: To seek the next qi, add to the large remainder fifteen, to the small remainder four hundred two, to the minute fraction eleven; when the minute fraction fills the qi divisor, carry to the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the era divisor, carry to the large remainder; per note [10], count as before: this is the next qi day.
translations.idiomatic: For each successive term add 15 days, 402 parts, and 11 minute-fractions, carrying overflows as prescribed; per note [10], index the result as before to name the next solar term.

sentences.zh: 推閏月術曰：以閏餘減章歲，餘以歲中乘之，滿章閏得一月，餘滿半法以上亦得一月。

translations.literal: Method for seeking the intercalary month: subtract the intercalary remainder from rule years; multiply the remainder by years per qi; divide by rule intercalations for one month; if the remainder fills half the divisor or more, again obtain one month.
