sentences.zh: 推沒滅術曰：因冬至積日有小餘者，加積一，以沒分乘之，以沒法除之，所得為大餘，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: Method for computing extinction and disappearance days: if the accumulated days from the winter solstice have a small remainder, add one to the accumulation; multiply by the extinction fraction and divide by the extinction divisor; the quotient is the large remainder, and what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find extinction and disappearance days: when the winter-solstice day count carries a fractional remainder, increment the day total by one, multiply by 67,315, divide by 967 for the sexagenary day line, and keep the residue as the fractional part.

sentences.zh: 大餘滿六十去之，餘命以紀，算外，即去年冬至後沒日也。

translations.literal: Remove sixty from the large remainder; count the remainder by the era, outside the reckoning: this is the extinction day after last year's winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the day line modulo sixty, index it against the sexagenary cycle, and the result names the first extinction day after the prior year's winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 求次沒，加大餘六十九，小餘五百九十二，小餘滿沒法得一，從大餘，命如前。

translations.literal: To seek the next extinction day, add to the large remainder sixty-nine and to the small remainder five hundred ninety-two; when the small remainder fills the extinction divisor, obtain one and carry to the large remainder; count as before.
translations.idiomatic: For each subsequent extinction day add 69 to the day count and 592 to the fraction, carrying overflow by 967 into the day count, then read off the date as before.

translations.literal: When the small remainder is exhausted, that is an extinction day.
translations.idiomatic: When the fractional part reaches zero, the day is a full extinction day rather than a mere disappearance day.

sentences.zh: 推五行用事日：立春、立夏、立秋、立冬者，即木、火、金、水始用事日也。

translations.literal: To compute the days when the Five Phases take effect: the days of Establishing Spring, Establishing Summer, Establishing Autumn, and Establishing Winter are respectively the days when Wood, Fire, Metal, and Water first take effect.
translations.idiomatic: The days when Wood, Fire, Metal, and Water begin to govern are found at Establishing Spring, Establishing Summer, Establishing Autumn, and Establishing Winter.

sentences.zh: 各減其大餘十八，小餘四百八十三，小分六，餘命以紀，算外，各四立之前土用事日也。

translations.literal: From each, subtract from the large remainder eighteen, from the small remainder four hundred eighty-three, and from the minute fraction six; count the remainder by the era, outside the reckoning: these are the days when Earth takes effect before each of the four establishments.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract 18 days, 483 parts, and 6 minute-fractions from each of those four dates, then index the result to obtain Earth's governing day immediately before each seasonal establishment.

translations.literal: If the large remainder is insufficient to subtract, add sixty.
translations.idiomatic: If the day count is too small, add 60 before subtracting.

sentences.zh: 小餘不足減者，減大餘一，加紀法；

translations.literal: If the small remainder is insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the large remainder and add the era divisor.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional part is too small, borrow one day and add 1,843 to the fraction.

sentences.zh: 小分不足減者，減小餘一，加氣法。

translations.literal: If the minute fraction is insufficient to subtract, subtract one from the small remainder and add the qi divisor.
translations.idiomatic: If the minute-fraction falls short, borrow one fractional unit and add 12 to the small remainder.

sentences.zh: 推卦用事日：因冬至大餘，六其小餘，坎卦用事日也。

translations.literal: To compute the days when hexagrams take effect: from the winter-solstice large remainder, multiply its small remainder by six: this is the day when the Kan hexagram takes effect.
translations.idiomatic: For hexagram rulership days, take the winter-solstice sexagenary line and multiply its fractional part by six to fix the day when Kan governs.

sentences.zh: 加小餘萬九十一，滿元法從大餘，即中孚用事日也。

translations.literal: Add to the small remainder ten thousand ninety-one; when it fills the origin divisor, carry to the large remainder: this is the day when Zhong Fu takes effect.
translations.idiomatic: Add 10,091 to the fractional part, carrying overflow by 11,058 into the day count, to reach the day when Zhong Fu governs.

sentences.zh: 求次卦，各加大餘六，小餘九百六十七。

translations.literal: To seek the next hexagram, add to each the large remainder six and the small remainder nine hundred sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Advance each subsequent hexagram by adding 6 to the day count and 967 to the fractional part.

sentences.zh: 其四正各因其中日，六其小餘。

translations.literal: For each of the four cardinal hexagrams, take its median day and multiply its small remainder by six.
translations.idiomatic: For the four cardinal hexagrams, use each one's midpoint day and multiply its fractional part by six.

sentences.zh: 推日度術曰：以紀法乘朔積日，滿周天去之，餘以紀法除之，所得為度，不盡為分。

translations.literal: Method for computing solar longitude: multiply accumulated new-moon days by the era divisor; remove what fills the circuit of heaven; divide the remainder by the era divisor—the quotient is degrees, and what does not exhaust is fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: To find the sun's ecliptic longitude, multiply accumulated conjunction days by 1,843, reduce modulo 673,150, then divide by 1,843 for whole degrees and keep the residue as arc-minutes.

sentences.zh: 命度從牛前五起，宿次除之，不滿宿，則天正十一月朔夜半日所在度及分也。

translations.literal: Count the degrees starting five lodges before Ox; remove lodge by lodge in sequence; what does not fill a lodge is then the degree and fractional parts where the sun stands at midnight on the new moon of the eleventh civil month of the celestial-standard year.
translations.idiomatic: Index the result from five lodges before Ox through the twenty-eight lodges; the remainder gives the sun's longitude at midnight on the eleventh month's conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求次日，日加一度，分不加，經斗除斗分，分少退一度。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, add one degree to the day without adding to the fractional parts; when passing through Dipper, remove the Dipper fraction; if the fractional parts are few, retreat one degree.
translations.idiomatic: For each following day add one degree without adding fractional parts; when crossing the Dipper lodge subtract its special fraction, and if the fraction is too small, step back one degree.

sentences.zh: 推月度術曰：以月周乘朔積日，滿周天去之，餘以紀法除之，所得為度，不盡為分，命如上法，則天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分也。

translations.literal: Method for computing lunar longitude: multiply accumulated new-moon days by the lunar circuit; remove what fills the circuit of heaven; divide the remainder by the era divisor—the quotient is degrees and what does not exhaust is fractional parts; count by the method above: then this is the degree and fractional parts where the moon stands at midnight on the new moon of the eleventh civil month of the celestial-standard year.
translations.idiomatic: To find the moon's longitude at the eleventh month's conjunction midnight, multiply accumulated days by 24,638, reduce modulo 673,150, divide by 1,843 for degrees and fractional parts, and index through the lodges as above.

sentences.zh: 求次月，小月加度二十二，分八百六；

translations.literal: To seek the next month, in a short month add twenty-two degrees and eight hundred six fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: For a short month add 22 degrees and 806 fractional parts to the moon's position.

sentences.zh: 大月又加一日，度十三，分六百七十九；

translations.literal: In a long month add another day, thirteen degrees, and six hundred seventy-nine fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: For a long month add one day, 13 degrees, and 679 fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 分滿紀法得一度，則次月朔夜半月所在度及分也。

translations.literal: When fractional parts fill the era divisor, obtain one degree: then this is the degree and fractional parts where the moon stands at midnight on the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Carry every 1,843 fractional parts into one degree to obtain the moon's longitude at the next conjunction midnight.

sentences.zh: 其冬下旬，月在張心署之。

translations.literal: In the late part of winter, when the moon is in Zhang or Heart, mark it.
translations.idiomatic: During the last ten days of winter, make a special notation whenever the moon stands in Zhang or Heart.

translations.literal: Editorial note 19.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 19.

sentences.zh: 推合朔度術曰：以章歲乘朔小餘，滿通法為大分，不盡為小分。

translations.literal: Method for computing the longitude of conjunction: multiply the new-moon small remainder by rule years; what fills the communication divisor becomes large fractional parts, and what does not exhaust is small fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: To find the longitude of syzygy, multiply the conjunction fractional day by 19; divide by 47 for large fractional parts and keep the remainder as small fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 以大分從朔夜半日度分，分滿紀法從度，[20]命如前，則天正十一月合朔日月所共合度也。

translations.literal: Let the large fractional parts follow the sun's degree and fractional parts at midnight on the new moon; when fractional parts fill the era divisor, carry to degrees; per note [20], count as before: then this is the common degree where sun and moon conjoin at the new moon of the eleventh civil month of the celestial-standard year.
translations.idiomatic: Add the large fractional parts to the sun's midnight longitude on conjunction day, carrying 1,843 fractional parts per degree; per note [20], index as before to fix the shared solar-lunar longitude for the eleventh month's syzygy.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加度二十九，大分九百七十七，小分四十二，小分滿通法從大分，大分滿紀法從度。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add twenty-nine degrees, nine hundred seventy-seven large fractional parts, and forty-two small fractional parts; when small fractional parts fill the communication divisor, carry to large fractional parts; when large fractional parts fill the era divisor, carry to degrees.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add 29 degrees, 977 large fractional parts, and 42 small fractional parts, propagating carries through the small-fraction, large-fraction, and degree levels.

sentences.zh: 經斗除其分，則次月合朔日月所共合度也。

translations.literal: When passing through Dipper, remove its fractional parts: then this is the common degree where sun and moon conjoin at the next month's new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the Dipper lodge's special fraction when crossing it to obtain the next month's syzygy longitude.

sentences.zh: 推弦望日所在度：加合朔度七，大分七百五，小分十，微分一，微分滿二從小分，小分滿通法從大分，大分滿紀法從度，命如前，則上弦日所在度也。

translations.literal: To compute the sun's longitude at first and third quarters and full moon: add to the conjunction longitude seven degrees, seven hundred five large fractional parts, ten small fractional parts, and one minute fraction; when minute fractions fill two, carry to small fractional parts; when small fractional parts fill the communication divisor, carry to large fractional parts; when large fractional parts fill the era divisor, carry to degrees; count as before: then this is the sun's longitude at first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: For the sun at first quarter, add 7 degrees, 705 large parts, 10 small parts, and 1 minute-fraction to the syzygy longitude, carrying overflows at each level, then index the result to name first quarter.

sentences.zh: 又加得望、下弦、後月合也。

translations.literal: Adding again, one obtains full moon, last quarter, and the next month's conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the same addition chain to reach full moon, third quarter, and the next syzygy.

sentences.zh: 推弦望月所在度：加合朔度九十八，大分千二百七十九，小分三十四，數滿命如前，即上弦月所在度也。

translations.literal: To compute the moon's longitude at first and third quarters and full moon: add to the conjunction longitude ninety-eight degrees, one thousand two hundred seventy-nine large fractional parts, and thirty-four small fractional parts; when the numbers fill, count as before: then this is the moon's longitude at first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: For the moon at first quarter, add 98 degrees, 1,279 large parts, and 34 small parts to the syzygy longitude, carrying overflows and indexing as before.

sentences.zh: 又加得望下弦後月合也。

translations.literal: Adding again, one obtains full moon, last quarter, and the next month's conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat the addition to reach full moon, third quarter, and the next syzygy.

sentences.zh: 推日月昏明度術曰：日以紀法，月以月周，乘所近節氣夜漏，二百而一，為明分。

translations.literal: Method for computing the degrees of sun and moon at dusk and dawn: for the sun multiply by the era divisor, for the moon multiply by the lunar circuit, multiply by the night clepsydra of the nearest solar term, and divide by two hundred to obtain the dawn fraction.
translations.idiomatic: To find dusk and dawn longitudes, multiply the era divisor for the sun or the lunar circuit for the moon by the nearest term's night water-clock reading, then divide by 200 for the dawn arc.

sentences.zh: 日以減紀法，月以減月周，餘為昏分。

translations.literal: For the sun subtract from the era divisor, for the moon subtract from the lunar circuit; the remainder is the dusk fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract that dawn arc from the era divisor for the sun or from the lunar circuit for the moon to obtain the dusk arc.

translations.literal: Add each to midnight and convert by the divisor to degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Add each arc to the midnight longitude and convert by the appropriate divisor to degrees.

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕術曰：置所入紀朔積分，以所入紀交會差率之數加之，以會通去之，餘則所求年天正十一月合朔去交度分也。

translations.literal: Method for computing conjunction, nodal crossing, and lunar eclipse: set the accumulated new-moon fraction for the era entered, add the eclipse-node difference rate for that era, remove what fills the nodal communication constant; the remainder is the degree and fractional parts by which the eleventh-month conjunction of the year sought stands from the node.
translations.idiomatic: To find nodal distance at syzygy, take the era's accumulated conjunction fraction, add its eclipse-node difference rate, reduce modulo 790,110, and the remainder is the eleventh-month conjunction's distance from the node.

sentences.zh: 以通數加之，滿會通去之，餘則次月合朔去交度分也。

translations.literal: Add the communication number; remove what fills the nodal communication constant; the remainder is the degree and fractional parts by which the next month's conjunction stands from the node.
translations.idiomatic: Add 134,630 and reduce modulo 790,110 to obtain the next month's nodal distance at conjunction.

sentences.zh: 以朔望合數各加其月合朔去交度分，滿會通去之，餘則各其月望去交度分也。

translations.literal: Add to each month's conjunction nodal distance the new-moon and full-moon conjunction number; remove what fills the nodal communication constant; the remainder is then each month's nodal distance at full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Add 67,315 to each month's conjunction nodal distance and reduce modulo 790,110 to fix the full-moon nodal distance for that month.

sentences.zh: 朔望去交分如朔望合數以下，[21]入交限數以上者，朔則交會，望則月蝕。

translations.literal: If the nodal distance at new moon or full moon is at or below the new-moon and full-moon conjunction number yet at or above the nodal-entry limit number, per note [21], then at new moon there is nodal crossing and at full moon there is lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When the nodal distance at syzygy or opposition falls between 67,315 and 722,795 inclusive, per note [21], the new moon crosses the node and the full moon brings a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕月在日道表裏術曰：置所入紀朔積分，以所入紀下交會差率之數加之，倍會通去之，餘不滿會通者，紀首表，天正合朔月在表，紀首裏，天正合朔月在裏。

translations.literal: Method for computing whether the moon at conjunction, nodal crossing, and lunar eclipse is north or south of the solar path: set the accumulated new-moon fraction for the era entered, add the lower eclipse-node difference rate for that era, remove twice what fills the nodal communication constant; if the remainder does not fill the nodal communication constant, at the era's head the moon is north and at the celestial-standard year's new moon the moon is north; at the era's head south, at the celestial-standard year's new moon the moon is south.
translations.idiomatic: To determine whether the moon lies north or south of the ecliptic, add the era's lower eclipse-node difference rate to its conjunction fraction, reduce modulo twice 790,110, and compare against 790,110: the era's opening polarity fixes whether the eleventh-month conjunction moon is north or south of the path.

sentences.zh: 滿會通去之，表在裏，裏在表。

translations.literal: Remove what fills the nodal communication constant: north becomes south and south becomes north.
translations.idiomatic: When the remainder crosses 790,110, north and south reverse.

sentences.zh: 求次月，以通數加之，滿會通去之，加裏滿在表，加表滿在裏。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add the communication number; remove what fills the nodal communication constant; if adding south fills, it is north; if adding north fills, it is south.
translations.idiomatic: For each following month add 134,630, reduce modulo 790,110, and flip polarity whenever the count crosses the nodal communication constant.

sentences.zh: 先交會後月蝕者，朔在表則望在表，朔在裏則望在裏。

translations.literal: When nodal crossing precedes lunar eclipse, if the new moon is north then the full moon is north; if the new moon is south then the full moon is south.
translations.idiomatic: If the node is crossed before the eclipse, new moon and full moon share the same side of the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 先月蝕後交會者，看食月朔在裏則望在表，朔在表則望在裏。

translations.literal: When lunar eclipse precedes nodal crossing, if the eclipsed new moon is south then the full moon is north; if the new moon is north then the full moon is south.
translations.idiomatic: If the eclipse comes before the nodal crossing, the full moon lies on the opposite side of the path from the new moon.

sentences.zh: 交會月蝕如朔望合數以下，[22]則前交後會；

translations.literal: If the nodal crossing and lunar eclipse are at or below the new-moon and full-moon conjunction number, per note [22], then the crossing precedes the eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When the nodal-eclipse value is at or below 67,315, per note [22], the node is crossed before the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 如入交限數以上，則前會後交。

translations.literal: If it is at or above the nodal-entry limit number, then the eclipse precedes the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the value reaches 722,795 or above, the eclipse precedes the nodal crossing.

sentences.zh: 其前交後會近於限數者，則豫伺之前月；

translations.literal: When crossing precedes eclipse and the value is close to the limit number, then watch the prior month in advance.
translations.idiomatic: If the node is crossed first and the value lies near the threshold, inspect the previous month as well.

sentences.zh: 前會後交近於限數者，則後伺之後月。

translations.literal: When eclipse precedes crossing and the value is close to the limit number, then watch the following month afterward.
translations.idiomatic: If the eclipse comes first and the value lies near the threshold, inspect the following month as well.

sentences.zh: 求去交度術曰：其前交後會者，今去交度分如日法而一，[23]所得則却去交度分也。

translations.literal: Method for finding the nodal distance: for cases where crossing precedes eclipse, divide the present nodal distance by the day divisor, per note [23]; the obtained value is the nodal distance retreated backward.
translations.idiomatic: To convert nodal distance when the node is crossed first, divide the current nodal distance by 4,559, per note [23], to obtain the distance measured back from the node.

sentences.zh: [24]其前會後交者，以去交度分減會通，餘如日法而一，所得則前去交度，餘皆度分也。

translations.literal: [24] For cases where eclipse precedes crossing, subtract the nodal distance from the nodal communication constant; divide the remainder by the day divisor; the obtained value is the nodal distance forward; the remainder is all in degrees and fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: [24] When the eclipse precedes the crossing, subtract the nodal distance from 790,110 and divide by 4,559; the quotient is the forward nodal distance, and any remainder stays in degrees and parts.

sentences.zh: 去交度十五以上，雖交不蝕也。

translations.literal: If the nodal distance is fifteen or more, even though there is crossing there is no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At a nodal distance of fifteen degrees or more, the bodies may cross the node but no eclipse occurs.

sentences.zh: 十以下是蝕，十以上虧蝕微少，光晷相及而已。

translations.literal: At ten or below there is eclipse; above ten the waning and eclipse are very slight—only the light's shadow reaches the other.
translations.idiomatic: At ten degrees or less a true eclipse occurs; above ten the obscuration is slight, with only the penumbra touching.

translations.literal: How much is waned is measured with fifteen as the divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Express the depth of obscuration as a fraction of fifteen.

sentences.zh: 求日蝕虧起角術曰：其月在外道，先交後會者，虧蝕西南角起；

translations.literal: Method for finding the corner from which solar eclipse waning begins: if the moon is on the outer path and crossing precedes eclipse, waning begins from the southwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: To find where a solar eclipse first bites: on the outer path with node crossed before eclipse, obscuration begins at the southwest limb.

sentences.zh: 先會後交者，虧蝕東南角起。

translations.literal: If eclipse precedes crossing, waning begins from the southeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: If the eclipse precedes the crossing, obscuration begins at the southeast limb.

sentences.zh: 其月在內道，先交後會者，虧食西北角起；

translations.literal: If the moon is on the inner path and crossing precedes eclipse, waning and eclipse begin from the northwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: On the inner path with crossing before eclipse, obscuration begins at the northwest limb.

sentences.zh: 先會後交者，虧食東北角起。

translations.literal: If eclipse precedes crossing, waning and eclipse begin from the northeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: If the eclipse precedes the crossing, obscuration begins at the northeast limb.

sentences.zh: 虧食分多少，如上以十五為法。

translations.literal: How much is waned and eclipsed is as above, with fifteen as the divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Measure the extent of obscuration as above, using fifteen as the divisor.

translations.literal: When crossing meets the center, the eclipse is total.
translations.idiomatic: When the node lies at the center, the eclipse is complete.

sentences.zh: 月蝕在日之衝，虧角與上反也。

translations.literal: A lunar eclipse is at the sun's opposite; the waning corner is the reverse of the above.
translations.idiomatic: A lunar eclipse occurs at opposition to the sun, and the corner of first obscuration is the mirror image of the solar case.

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕入遲疾曆術曰：置所入紀朔積分，以所入紀下遲疾差率之數加之，以通周去之，餘滿日法得一日，不盡為日餘，命日算外，則所求年天正十一月合朔入曆日也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing conjunction, nodal crossing, and lunar eclipse into the slow-fast calendar: set the accumulated new-moon fraction for the era entered; add the slow-fast difference rate listed under that era; remove multiples of the communication cycle; what fills the day divisor becomes one day, what does not exhaust is the day remainder; count days outside the reckoning: this is the day entered into the table at the eleventh-month conjunction of the year sought.
translations.idiomatic: To place a syzygy inside the lunar speed table: add the tabulated anomaly increment to the lunation fraction, reduce modulo 125,621, divide by 4,559 for whole days plus remainder, and index the result to name the anomaly day for the eleventh month's conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求次月，加一日，日餘四千四百五十。

translations.literal: To seek the next month, add one day, day remainder four thousand four hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: For the following month add one day and 4,450 day-fraction parts.

sentences.zh: [28]求望，加十四日，日餘三千四百八十九。

translations.literal: [28] To seek full moon, add fourteen days, day remainder three thousand four hundred eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Per note [28], for opposition add fourteen days and 3,489 fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 日餘滿日法成日，日滿二十七去之。

translations.literal: When day remainders fill the day divisor, they form a day; when days fill twenty-seven, remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Carry fractions into days at 4,559, then reduce full weeks of 27 days.

sentences.zh: 又除餘如周日餘，日餘不足除者，減一日，加周虛。

translations.literal: Again remove the remainder as with the cycle-day remainder; if the day remainder is insufficient for the division, subtract one day and add the cycle shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: If the fractional division underflows at the week boundary, borrow one day and add the weekly complement 2,031.

sentences.zh: 推合朔交會月蝕定大小餘：以入曆日餘，[29]乘所入曆損益率，以損益盈縮積分為定積分。

translations.literal: Method for fixing large and small remainders for conjunction, nodal crossing, and lunar eclipse: multiply the day remainder entered in the table, per note [29], by the excess-deficit rate for that entry, and with it increase or decrease the surplus-deficit accumulated parts to obtain the fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: Per note [29], to fix syzygy instants multiply the anomalistic day fraction by the tabulated rate and apply it to the surplus-deficit column for the corrected integral.

sentences.zh: 以章歲減所入曆月行分，餘以除之，所得以盈減縮加本小餘。

translations.literal: Subtract from rule years the lunar motion parts entered in the table; divide the remainder into it; what is obtained, subtract from surplus or add to shrinkage the original small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the adjusted integral by the difference between 19 and the tabulated motion parts, then subtract surplus or add shrinkage to the base fractional day.

sentences.zh: 加之滿日法者，交會加時在後日；

translations.literal: If adding fills the day divisor, the conjunction or crossing hour falls on the following day.
translations.idiomatic: A carry past the day divisor pushes the conjunction instant into the next civil day.

sentences.zh: 減之，不足者，交會加時在前日。

translations.literal: If subtracting is insufficient, the conjunction or crossing hour falls on the preceding day.
translations.idiomatic: A borrow moves the corrected instant onto the previous day.

sentences.zh: 月蝕者，隨定大小餘為日加時。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipses, follow the fixed large and small remainders as the day's double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipses take their clock time directly from the corrected remainder line.

sentences.zh: 入曆在周日者，以周日日餘乘縮積分，為定積分。

translations.literal: If entry falls on the cycle day, multiply shrinkage accumulated parts by the cycle-day remainder to obtain fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: At the anomalistic week boundary, multiply the deficit column by the weekly fractional day for the corrected integral.

sentences.zh: 以損率乘入曆日餘，[30]又以周日日餘乘之，以周日日度小分并之，以損定積分，餘為後定積分。

translations.literal: Multiply the deficit rate by the day remainder entered in the table, per note [30], again multiply by the cycle-day remainder, add the cycle-day degree micro-fraction, and with them decrease the fixed accumulated parts; the remainder is the later fixed accumulated parts.
translations.idiomatic: Per note [30], combine the rate product with weekly micro-parts to obtain the post-boundary correction stack.

sentences.zh: 以章歲減周日月行分，餘以周日日餘乘之，以周日度小分并之，以除後定積分，所得以加本小餘，如上法。

translations.literal: Subtract from rule years the moon's motion parts for the cycle week; multiply the remainder by the cycle-day remainder, add the cycle-week degree micro-fraction, divide into the later fixed accumulated parts; what is obtained, add to the original small remainder, as in the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Finish the week-crossing correction by dividing with the prescribed divisor mix, then add to the base fraction as above.

sentences.zh: 推加時：以十二乘定小餘，滿日法得一辰，數從子起，算外，則朔望加時所在辰也。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the double-hour: multiply the fixed small remainder by twelve; what fills the day divisor obtains one chen; count from zi outward, outside the reckoning: this is the chen where the new- or full-moon hour falls.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the corrected fraction by twelve and divide by 4,559 to name the twelve double-hours from midnight.

sentences.zh: 有餘不盡者四之，如日法而一為少，二為半，三為太。

translations.literal: If there is remainder not exhausted, quadruple it; divide by the day divisor to obtain shao, two makes ban, three makes tai.
translations.idiomatic: Split the leftover into quarters of the divisor for the shao, ban, and tai fine subdivisions.

sentences.zh: 又有餘者三之，如日法而一為強，半法以上排成之，不滿半法廢棄之。

translations.literal: If again there is remainder, triple it; divide by the day divisor to obtain qiang; if it fills half the divisor or more, advance it one notch; if it does not fill half the divisor, discard it.
translations.idiomatic: Further triple the tail to reach the strong step, rounding up at half-divisor.

sentences.zh: 以強并少為少強，并半為半強，并太為太強。

translations.literal: Combine qiang with shao to make shao-qiang; combine with ban to make ban-qiang; combine with tai to make tai-qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Add strong units to weak, half, or full subdivisions per the classical clepsydra notation.

sentences.zh: 得二強者為少弱，以之并少為半弱，以之并半為太弱，以之并太為一辰弱。

translations.literal: Obtaining two qiang makes shao-ruo; with it combine shao to make ban-ruo; with it combine ban to make tai-ruo; with it combine tai to make one chen-ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Two strongs collapse into a weak grade, stepping through the ladder to a full weak double-hour mark.

sentences.zh: 以所在辰命之，則各得其少、太、半及強、弱也。

translations.literal: Count by the chen where it stands, and each obtains its shao, tai, ban, and qiang, ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Read the final label against the stem hour to recover shao, tai, ban, qiang, and ruo.

sentences.zh: 其月蝕望在中節前後四日以還者，視限數；

translations.literal: If the lunar eclipse full moon lies within four days on either side of the mid-term node, consult the limit number.

translations.literal: If it lies five or more days before or after the mid-term node, consult the gap limit.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond five days from the major term, apply the wider gap-limit rule.

sentences.zh: 定小餘如間限、限數以下者，以算上為日。

translations.literal: If the fixed small remainder is at or below the gap limit and limit numbers, count upward and treat it as a day.

sentences.zh: 右中節二十四氣，如術求之，得冬至十一月中也。

translations.literal: The right-hand median nodes of the twenty-four qi—seek them by the method and you obtain the winter solstice in the middle of the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: The median terms listed at right are found by the procedure above; the first result is the winter solstice in the middle of the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 加之得次月節，加節得其月中。

translations.literal: Add to it and you obtain the next month's node; add the node and you obtain that month's median.
translations.idiomatic: Adding one step yields the next minor term; adding a minor term in turn yields the corresponding major term.

translations.literal: The median stars take the sun's position as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Culmination stars are reckoned from the sun's lodge position on the given day.

sentences.zh: 置所求年二十四氣小餘四之，如法得一為少，不盡少三之，如法為強。

translations.literal: Set the small remainder of the twenty-four qi for the year sought; quadruple it; divide by the divisor to obtain shao; what does not exhaust, triple it and divide by the divisor to obtain qiang.
translations.idiomatic: For the target year, take each solar term's fractional remainder, multiply by four and divide by the day divisor for shao units; triple the leftover and divide again for qiang units.

sentences.zh: 所得以減其節氣昏明中星各定。

translations.literal: What is obtained, subtract from each solar term's dusk and dawn median stars to fix them.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract those shao and qiang amounts from the tabulated dusk and dawn culmination stars to obtain the corrected values.

translations.literal: Editorial note 44.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 44.

translations.literal: Method for computing the five planets:
translations.idiomatic: Procedure for the five planets:

sentences.zh: 五星者，木曰歲星，火曰熒惑，土曰填星，金曰太白，水曰辰星。

translations.literal: The five planets: Wood is called the Year Star, Fire the Sparkling Deluder, Earth the Reimbursing Star, Metal the Great White, and Water the Chronogram Star.
translations.idiomatic: The five planets are Jupiter (Year Star), Mars (Sparkling Deluder), Saturn (Reimbursing Star), Venus (Great White), and Mercury (Chronogram Star).

sentences.zh: 凡五星之行，有遲有疾，有留有逆。

translations.literal: In general the motion of the five planets has slow and fast phases, halts and retrogrades.
translations.idiomatic: Each planet moves now slowly, now swiftly, sometimes halting and sometimes moving backward.

sentences.zh: 曩自開闢，清濁始分，則日月五星聚于星紀。

translations.literal: From the opening of the age, when clear and turbid first separated, the sun, moon, and five planets gathered in Star Chronogram.
translations.idiomatic: Since the world's beginning, when yin and yang first divided, the sun, moon, and five planets all clustered in the Star Chronogram lodge.

sentences.zh: 發自星紀，並而行天，遲疾留逆，互相逮及。

translations.literal: Issuing from Star Chronogram, they proceed together through Heaven; slow, fast, halt, and retrograde mutually overtake one another.
translations.idiomatic: Starting from Star Chronogram they travel the sky in concert, their slow, fast, stationary, and retrograde motions continually catching and passing one another.

sentences.zh: 星與日會，同宿共度，則謂之合。

translations.literal: When a star meets the sun in the same lodge and the same degree, this is called a conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: When a planet and the sun share the same lodge and degree, the event is termed a conjunction.

sentences.zh: 從合至合之日，則謂之終。

translations.literal: From the day of one conjunction to the day of the next conjunction is called one cycle.
translations.idiomatic: The interval from one conjunction day to the next is one complete planetary cycle.

sentences.zh: 各以一終之日與一歲之日，通分相約，終而率之，歲數歲則謂之合終歲數，歲終則謂之合終合數。

translations.literal: For each, compare one cycle-day with one year's days by reducing them to a common denominator; taking the cycle as the rate, the year-count is called the total cycle year-count, and the cycle-count is called the total cycle conjunction-count.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce each planet's cycle length and the civil year to a common fractional base; the resulting year ratio is the total cycle year-count and the conjunction ratio is the total cycle conjunction-count.

translations.literal: Editorial note 45.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 45.

translations.literal: Once the two rates are fixed, the divisor numbers are generated.
translations.idiomatic: With both rates established, the computational divisors follow.

sentences.zh: 以章歲乘合數為合月法，以紀法乘合數為日度法，以章月乘歲數為合月分，如合月法為合月數，合月之餘為月餘。

translations.literal: Multiply the conjunction-count by rule years to obtain the conjunction-month divisor; multiply the conjunction-count by era divisor to obtain the day-degree divisor; multiply the year-count by rule months to obtain the conjunction-month parts; divide by the conjunction-month divisor for the conjunction-month count, and the remainder of the conjunction month is the month remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Form the conjunction-month divisor by rule years times conjunction-count, the day-degree divisor by era divisor times conjunction-count, and conjunction-month parts by rule months times year-count; divide for whole conjunction months and keep the remainder as month remainder.

sentences.zh: 以通數乘合月數，如日法而一為大餘，以六十去大餘，餘為星合朔大餘。

translations.literal: Multiply the conjunction-month count by the communication number; divide by the day divisor to obtain the large remainder; remove sixty from the large remainder—the remainder is the large remainder of the star's conjunction new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply conjunction months by the communication number, divide by the day divisor for the sexagenary line, reduce modulo sixty, and the result is the star-conjunction new-moon large remainder.

translations.literal: The remainder of the large remainder is the new-moon small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: What remains after the sexagenary reduction is the new-moon small remainder.

sentences.zh: [46]以通數乘月餘，以合月法乘朔小餘，并之，以日法乘合月法除之，所得星合入月日數也。

translations.literal: [46] Multiply the month remainder by the communication number; multiply the new-moon small remainder by the conjunction-month divisor; combine them and divide by the day divisor multiplied by the conjunction-month divisor—the obtained value is the number of days the star's conjunction enters the month.
translations.idiomatic: Per note [46], combine month remainder and new-moon fraction with the prescribed divisors; the quotient is the day-count on which the planetary conjunction enters the lunar month.

sentences.zh: 餘以通法約之，[47]為入月日餘。

translations.literal: Reduce the remainder by the communication divisor; [47] this is the day remainder entered in the month.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the leftover by the communication divisor; per note [47], the result is the fractional day remainder within the month.

sentences.zh: [48]以朔小餘減日法，餘為朔虛分。

translations.literal: [48] Subtract the new-moon small remainder from the day divisor; the remainder is the new-moon void fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Per note [48], subtract the new-moon small remainder from the day divisor; the difference is the new-moon void fraction.

sentences.zh: 以曆斗分乘合數，為星度斗分。

translations.literal: Multiply the calendrical dipper fraction by the conjunction-count to obtain the star-degree dipper fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the calendar's dipper fraction by the conjunction-count to obtain the planetary dipper fraction.

sentences.zh: 木、火、土各以合數減歲數，餘以周天乘之，如日度法而一，所得則行星度數也，餘則度餘。

translations.literal: For Wood, Fire, and Earth, subtract the conjunction-count from the year-count for each; multiply the remainder by the circuit of heaven and divide by the day-degree divisor—the obtained value is the planetary degree count, and the remainder is the degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn, subtract the conjunction-count from the year-count, multiply by the circuit-of-heaven constant, divide by the day-degree divisor for whole degrees, and keep the remainder as degree remainder.

sentences.zh: 金、水以周天乘歲數，如日度法而一，所得則行星度數也，餘則度餘。

translations.literal: For Metal and Water, multiply the year-count by the circuit of heaven and divide by the day-degree divisor—the obtained value is the planetary degree count, and the remainder is the degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, multiply the year-count by the circuit-of-heaven constant and divide by the day-degree divisor for degrees and degree remainder.
