sentences.zh: 推五星術曰：置壬辰元以來盡所求年，以合終合數乘之，滿合終歲數得一，名積合，不盡名合餘。

translations.literal: Method for pushing the five planets says: set the years elapsed since the Renchen origin, multiply by the total cycle conjunction-count; divide by the total cycle year-count to obtain one—this is called accumulated conjunction; what does not exhaust is called conjunction remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The procedure for the five planets runs thus: take the years since the Renchen origin, multiply by the total cycle conjunction-count, and divide by the total cycle year-count; the quotient is the accumulated conjunction, the remainder the conjunction surplus.

sentences.zh: 以合終合數減合餘，得一者星合往年，得二者合前往年，無所得，合其年。

translations.literal: Subtract the conjunction remainder from the total cycle conjunction-count; if one is obtained the star conjoined in the preceding year, if two in the year before that; if nothing is obtained, it conjoined in the current year.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the conjunction remainder from the total cycle conjunction-count: a result of one places the conjunction in the prior year, of two in the year before that; if nothing remains, the conjunction falls in the year sought.

sentences.zh: 餘以減合終合數，為度分。

translations.literal: Subtract the remainder from the total cycle conjunction-count; this is the degree fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract that remainder from the total cycle conjunction-count to obtain the degree fraction.

sentences.zh: 金、水積合，偶為晨，奇為夕。

translations.literal: For accumulated conjunctions of Metal and Water, even means morning, odd means evening.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, an even accumulated conjunction marks a morning appearance, an odd one an evening appearance.

sentences.zh: 推五星合月：以月數月餘各乘積合，餘滿合月法從月，為積月，不盡為月餘。

translations.literal: To push the five-star conjunction month: multiply month count and month remainder each by the accumulated conjunction; when the remainder fills the conjunction-month divisor, add to the month count for accumulated months; what does not exhaust is the month remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To find the conjunction month, multiply both the month count and month remainder by the accumulated conjunction; carry into whole months whenever the remainder fills the conjunction-month divisor, and keep the leftover as month remainder.

sentences.zh: 以紀月除積月，所得算外，所入紀也，餘為入紀月。

translations.literal: Divide accumulated months by era months; the count outside the reckoning is the era entered, and the remainder is the month entered in the era.
translations.idiomatic: Divide accumulated months by the era month-total; the quotient names the era entered and the remainder the month within that era.

sentences.zh: 副以章閏乘之，[51]滿章月得一為閏，以減入紀月，餘以歲中去之，餘為入歲月，命以天正起，算外，星合月也。

translations.literal: Auxiliary: multiply by rule intercalations; [51] when it fills rule months obtain one as intercalation; subtract intercalation from the month entered in the era; remove years from the remainder; the remainder is the month entered in the year; count from the celestial first month outside the reckoning—this is the star-conjunction month.
translations.idiomatic: Then multiply the auxiliary by rule intercalations; per note [51], divide by rule months for whole intercalary months, subtract them from the era month, remove full years from what remains, and index from the celestial first month—the result is the star-conjunction month.

translations.literal: When this falls at an intercalary junction, use the new moon to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: If the date falls at an intercalary boundary, govern it by the nearest new moon.

sentences.zh: 推合月朔：以通數乘入紀月，滿日法得一為積日，不盡為小餘。

translations.literal: To push the conjunction-month new moon: multiply the month entered in the era by the communication number; divide by the day divisor to obtain one as accumulated days; what does not exhaust is the small remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To obtain the conjunction new moon, multiply the era month by the communication number, divide by the day divisor for accumulated days, and keep the remainder as the small fraction.

sentences.zh: 以六十去積日，餘為大餘，命以所入紀，算外，星合朔日也。

translations.literal: Remove sixty from accumulated days; the remainder is the large remainder; count from the era entered outside the reckoning—this is the star-conjunction new-moon day.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce accumulated days modulo sixty for the sexagenary remainder, index from the era entered, and the result is the star-conjunction new-moon day.

sentences.zh: 推入月日：以通數乘月餘，合月法乘朔小餘，并之，通法約之，所得滿日度法得一，則星合入月日也，不滿為日餘。

translations.literal: To push the day entered in the month: multiply the month remainder by the communication number; multiply the new-moon small remainder by the conjunction-month divisor; combine them and reduce by the communication divisor; when the obtained value fills the day-degree divisor obtain one—then this is the day the star-conjunction enters the month; what does not fill is the day remainder.
translations.idiomatic: For the day within the month, combine month remainder and new-moon fraction through the communication and conjunction divisors; divide by the day-degree divisor for the entry day, keeping any remainder as day surplus.

sentences.zh: 命日以朔，算外，入月日也。

translations.literal: Count the day from the new moon outside the reckoning—this is the day entered in the month.
translations.idiomatic: Index that day from the new moon outside the reckoning to name the day entered in the month.

sentences.zh: 推星合度：以周天乘度分，滿日度法得一為度，不盡為餘，命以牛前五度起，算外，星所合度也。

translations.literal: To push the star-conjunction degree: multiply the circuit of heaven by the degree fraction; divide by the day-degree divisor to obtain one as a degree; what does not exhaust is the remainder; count from five degrees before Ox outside the reckoning—this is the degree at which the star conjoins.
translations.idiomatic: For the conjunction degree, multiply the circuit of heaven by the degree fraction and divide by the day-degree divisor; index from five degrees before Ox to obtain the lodge and degree of conjunction.

sentences.zh: 求後合月，以月數加入歲月，以餘加月餘，餘滿合月法得一月，月不滿歲中，即在其年；

translations.literal: To seek the next conjunction month, add the month count to the month entered in the year and add the remainder to the month remainder; when the remainder fills the conjunction-month divisor obtain one month; if the month does not fill the year, it is in that year;
translations.idiomatic: To find the next conjunction month, add the tabulated month count and remainder to the current year-month; carry a month whenever the remainder fills the conjunction-month divisor—if the month still lies within the year, the conjunction falls in that year;

sentences.zh: 滿去之，有閏計焉，餘為後年；

translations.literal: when it fills, remove it; if intercalation is counted, the remainder is the following year;
translations.idiomatic: otherwise remove full years, accounting for intercalation, and the remainder points to a later year;

translations.literal: when it fills again, it is in the second year thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: if it fills once more, the conjunction lies two years ahead.

sentences.zh: 金、水加晨得夕，加夕得晨也。

translations.literal: For Metal and Water, adding morning yields evening, adding evening yields morning.
translations.idiomatic: For Venus and Mercury, adding to a morning date yields an evening one, and adding to an evening date yields a morning one.

sentences.zh: 求後合朔，以朔大小餘數加合朔月大小餘，其月餘上成月者，又加大餘二十九，小餘二千四百一十九。

translations.literal: To seek the next conjunction new moon, add the new-moon large and small remainder numbers to the large and small remainders of the conjunction month; when the month remainder carries into a full month, also add large remainder twenty-nine and small remainder two thousand four hundred nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: For the next conjunction new moon, add the tabulated new-moon remainders to those of the conjunction month, and when the month fraction carries a month, also add twenty-nine to the large remainder and 2,419 to the small.

sentences.zh: [52]小餘滿日法從大餘，命如前法。

translations.literal: [52] When the small remainder fills the day divisor, carry to the large remainder; count by the method above.
translations.idiomatic: Per note [52], carry from small to large remainder when the small fraction fills the day divisor, then index as before.

sentences.zh: 求後入月日，[53]以入月日、日餘加入月日及餘，[54]餘滿日度法得一。

translations.literal: To seek the next day entered in the month, [53] add the day entered in the month and day remainder to the day entered in the month and remainder; [54] when the remainder fills the day-degree divisor obtain one.
translations.idiomatic: Per note [53], add the tabulated entry day and day remainder to the current ones; per note [54], carry a day whenever the remainder fills the day-degree divisor.

sentences.zh: 其前合朔小餘滿其虛分者，去一日；

translations.literal: If the prior conjunction new-moon small remainder fills its void fraction, remove one day;
translations.idiomatic: If the preceding conjunction new-moon small remainder fills its void fraction, subtract one day;

sentences.zh: 後小餘滿二千四百一十九以上，去二十九日；

translations.literal: if the later small remainder is two thousand four hundred nineteen or more, remove twenty-nine days;
translations.idiomatic: if the later small remainder reaches 2,419 or above, subtract twenty-nine days;

sentences.zh: 不滿，去三十日，其餘則後合入月日，命以朔。

translations.literal: if it does not fill, remove thirty days; the remainder is then the next conjunction day entered in the month; count from the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise subtract thirty days; what remains is the next conjunction day within the month, indexed from the new moon.

sentences.zh: 求後合度，以度數及分，如前合宿次命之。

translations.literal: To seek the next conjunction degree, add the degree count and fraction and count the lodge sequence as at the prior conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: For the next conjunction degree, add the tabulated degree and fraction and index the lodge sequence as before.

sentences.zh: 木：晨與日合，伏，順，十六日九十九萬七千八百三十二分，行星二度百七十九萬五千二百三十八分，而晨見東方，在日後。

translations.literal: Wood: at dawn conjoined with the sun, it hides; prograde, sixteen days and nine hundred ninety-seven thousand eight hundred thirty-two fractional parts, traversing two degrees and one million seven hundred ninety-five thousand two hundred thirty-eight fractional parts, then at dawn appears in the east, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter: conjoined with the sun at dawn, it disappears; moving prograde for sixteen days plus 997,832 fractional parts and two degrees plus 1,795,238 fractional parts, it reappears in the east at dawn, behind the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行五十七分之十一，五十七日行十一度。

translations.literal: Prograde, swift: daily motion eleven parts in fifty-seven; in fifty-seven days it moves eleven degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde and swift: it advances eleven parts per fifty-seven each day, eleven degrees in fifty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 順，遲，日行九分，五十七日行九度而留。

translations.literal: Prograde, slow: daily motion nine parts; in fifty-seven days it moves nine degrees and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde and slow: nine parts per day, nine degrees in fifty-seven days, then it stops.

translations.literal: Stationary, twenty-seven days, then turns back.
translations.idiomatic: It remains motionless for twenty-seven days, then reverses.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行七分之一，八十四日退十二度，而復留二十七日。

translations.literal: Retrograde: daily motion one part in seven; in eighty-four days it retreats twelve degrees, then halts again for twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde: one part in seven per day, twelve degrees back in eighty-four days, then another twenty-seven-day halt.

sentences.zh: 復遲，日行九分，五十七日行九度而復順。

translations.literal: Again slow, daily motion nine parts; in fifty-seven days it moves nine degrees, then again prograde.
translations.idiomatic: Slow again at nine parts per day, nine degrees in fifty-seven days, then prograde once more.

sentences.zh: 疾，日行十一分，五十七日行十一度，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Swift: daily motion eleven parts; in fifty-seven days it moves eleven degrees; ahead of the sun, it hides in the west at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Swift motion at eleven parts per day, eleven degrees in fifty-seven days; standing ahead of the sun, it sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 順，十六日九十九萬七千八百三十二分，行星二度百七十九萬五千二百三十八分，而與日合。

translations.literal: Prograde, sixteen days and nine hundred ninety-seven thousand eight hundred thirty-two fractional parts, traversing two degrees and one million seven hundred ninety-five thousand two hundred thirty-eight fractional parts, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde for sixteen days plus 997,832 fractional parts and two degrees plus 1,795,238 fractional parts, then it conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 凡一終，三百九十八日百九十九萬五千六百六十四分，行星三十三度百四十七萬二千八百六十九分。

translations.literal: In all one cycle: three hundred ninety-eight days and one million nine hundred ninety-five thousand six hundred sixty-four fractional parts; planetary motion thirty-three degrees and one million four hundred seventy-two thousand eight hundred sixty-nine fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: One complete cycle: 398 days plus 1,995,664 fractional parts; planetary travel 33 degrees plus 1,472,869 fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 火：晨與日合，伏，七十二日百七十九萬二千六百一十五分，行星五十六度百二十四萬九千三百四十五分，而晨見東方，在日後。

translations.literal: Fire: at dawn conjoined with the sun, it hides; seventy-two days and one million seven hundred ninety-two thousand six hundred fifteen fractional parts, traversing fifty-six degrees and one million two hundred forty-nine thousand three hundred forty-five fractional parts, then at dawn appears in the east, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Mars: conjoined with the sun at dawn, it disappears; after seventy-two days plus 1,792,615 fractional parts and fifty-six degrees plus 1,249,345 fractional parts, it reappears in the east at dawn, behind the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，日行二十三分之十四，百八十四日行百一十二度。

translations.literal: Prograde: daily motion fourteen parts in twenty-three; in one hundred eighty-four days it moves one hundred twelve degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde: fourteen parts in twenty-three per day, one hundred twelve degrees in one hundred eighty-four days.

sentences.zh: 更順，遲，日行十二分，九十二日行四十八度而留。

translations.literal: Again prograde, slow: daily motion twelve parts; in ninety-two days it moves forty-eight degrees and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde and slow again: twelve parts per day, forty-eight degrees in ninety-two days, then it stops.

translations.literal: Stationary, eleven days, then turns back.
translations.idiomatic: Motionless for eleven days, then it reverses.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行六十二分之十七，六十二日退十七度，而復留十一日。

translations.literal: Retrograde: daily motion seventeen parts in sixty-two; in sixty-two days it retreats seventeen degrees, then halts again for eleven days.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde: seventeen parts in sixty-two per day, seventeen degrees back in sixty-two days, then another eleven-day halt.

sentences.zh: 復順，遲，日行十二分，九十二日，行四十八度而復疾。

translations.literal: Again prograde, slow: daily motion twelve parts; in ninety-two days it moves forty-eight degrees, then again swift.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde and slow again: twelve parts per day, forty-eight degrees in ninety-two days, then swift motion resumes.

sentences.zh: 日行十四分，百八十四日行百一十二度，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Daily motion fourteen parts; in one hundred eighty-four days it moves one hundred twelve degrees; ahead of the sun, it hides in the west at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen parts per day, one hundred twelve degrees in one hundred eighty-four days; ahead of the sun, it sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 順，七十二日百七十九萬二千六百一十五分，行星五十六度百二十四萬九千三百四十五分，而與日合。

translations.literal: Prograde, seventy-two days and one million seven hundred ninety-two thousand six hundred fifteen fractional parts, traversing fifty-six degrees and one million two hundred forty-nine thousand three hundred forty-five fractional parts, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde for seventy-two days plus 1,792,615 fractional parts and fifty-six degrees plus 1,249,345 fractional parts, then it conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 凡一終，七百八十日三百五十八萬五千二百三十分，行星四百一十五度二百四十九萬八千六百九十分。

translations.literal: In all one cycle: seven hundred eighty days and three million five hundred eighty-five thousand two hundred thirty fractional parts; planetary motion four hundred fifteen degrees and two million four hundred ninety-eight thousand six hundred ninety fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: One complete cycle: 780 days plus 3,585,230 fractional parts; planetary travel 415 degrees plus 2,498,690 fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 土：晨與日合，伏，十九日三百八十四萬七千六百七十五分半，行星二度六百四十九萬一千一百二十一分半，而晨見東方，在日後。

translations.literal: Earth: at dawn conjoined with the sun, it hides; nineteen days and three million eight hundred forty-seven thousand six hundred seventy-five and a half fractional parts, traversing two degrees and six million four hundred ninety-one thousand one hundred twenty-one and a half fractional parts, then at dawn appears in the east, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn: conjoined with the sun at dawn, it disappears; after nineteen days plus 3,847,675½ fractional parts and two degrees plus 6,491,121½ fractional parts, it reappears in the east at dawn, behind the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，行百七十二分之十三，八十六日行六度半而留。

translations.literal: Prograde: motion thirteen parts in one hundred seventy-two; in eighty-six days it moves six and a half degrees and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde: thirteen parts in 172 per day, six and a half degrees in eighty-six days, then it stops.

translations.literal: Stationary, thirty-two and a half days, then turns back.
translations.idiomatic: Motionless for thirty-two and a half days, then it reverses.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行十七分之一，百二日退六度而復留。

translations.literal: Retrograde: daily motion one part in seventeen; in one hundred two days it retreats six degrees, then halts again.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde: one part in seventeen per day, six degrees back in one hundred two days, then another halt.

sentences.zh: 不行，三十二日半復順，日行十三分，八十六日行六度半，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Stationary, thirty-two and a half days; again prograde, daily motion thirteen parts; in eighty-six days it moves six and a half degrees; ahead of the sun, it hides in the west at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty-two and a half motionless days it turns prograde again at thirteen parts per day, six and a half degrees in eighty-six days; ahead of the sun, it sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 順，十九日三百八十四萬七千六百七十五分半，行星二度六百四十九萬一千一百二十一分半，而與日合。

translations.literal: Prograde, nineteen days and three million eight hundred forty-seven thousand six hundred seventy-five and a half fractional parts, traversing two degrees and six million four hundred ninety-one thousand one hundred twenty-one and a half fractional parts, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde for nineteen days plus 3,847,675½ fractional parts and two degrees plus 6,491,121½ fractional parts, then it conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 凡一終，三百七十八日六十七萬五千三百六十四分，行星十二度五百九十六萬二千二百五十六分。

translations.literal: In all one cycle: three hundred seventy-eight days and six hundred seventy-five thousand three hundred sixty-four fractional parts; planetary motion twelve degrees and five million nine hundred sixty-two thousand two hundred fifty-six fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: One complete cycle: 378 days plus 675,364 fractional parts; planetary travel 12 degrees plus 5,962,256 fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 金：晨與日合，伏，六日退四度，而晨見東方，在日後而逆。

translations.literal: Metal: at dawn conjoined with the sun, it hides; six days retreating four degrees, then at dawn appears in the east, behind the sun and retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: Venus: conjoined with the sun at dawn, it disappears; after six days retreating four degrees it reappears in the east at dawn, behind the sun and moving backward.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行五分之三，十日退六度。

translations.literal: Slow retrograde: daily motion three parts in five; in ten days it retreats six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Slow and retrograde: three parts in five per day, six degrees back in ten days.

translations.literal: Stationary, seven days, then turns back.
translations.idiomatic: Motionless for seven days, then it reverses.

sentences.zh: 順，遲，日行四十五分之三十三，四十五日行三十三度而順。

translations.literal: Prograde, slow: daily motion thirty-three parts in forty-five; in forty-five days it moves thirty-three degrees, then prograde.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde and slow: thirty-three parts in forty-five per day, thirty-three degrees in forty-five days, then faster prograde.

sentences.zh: 疾，日行一度九十一分之十四，九十一日行百五度而順。

translations.literal: Swift: daily motion one degree and fourteen parts in ninety-one; in ninety-one days it moves one hundred five degrees, then prograde.
translations.idiomatic: Swift: one degree plus fourteen parts in ninety-one per day, one hundred five degrees in ninety-one days, still prograde.

sentences.zh: 益疾，日行一度九十一分之二十一，九十一日行百一十二度，在日後，而晨伏東方。

translations.literal: Increasingly swift: daily motion one degree and twenty-one parts in ninety-one; in ninety-one days it moves one hundred twelve degrees; behind the sun, it hides in the east at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Still faster: one degree plus twenty-one parts in ninety-one per day, one hundred twelve degrees in ninety-one days; behind the sun, it vanishes in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 順，四十二日十九萬四千九百九十分，行星五十二度十九萬四千九百九十分，而與日合。

translations.literal: Prograde, forty-two days and one hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred ninety fractional parts, traversing fifty-two degrees and one hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred ninety fractional parts, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde for forty-two days plus 194,990 fractional parts and fifty-two degrees plus 194,990 fractional parts, then it conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 一合，二百九十二日十九萬四千九百九十分，行星如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: two hundred ninety-two days and one hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred ninety fractional parts; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One conjunction: 292 days plus 194,990 fractional parts; planetary travel the same.

sentences.zh: 金：夕與日合，伏，順，四十二日十九萬四千九百九十分，行星五十二度十九萬四千九百九十分，而夕見西方，在日前。

translations.literal: Metal: at dusk conjoined with the sun, it hides; prograde, forty-two days and one hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred ninety fractional parts, traversing fifty-two degrees and one hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred ninety fractional parts, then at dusk appears in the west, ahead of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Venus: conjoined with the sun at dusk, it disappears; prograde for forty-two days plus 194,990 fractional parts and fifty-two degrees plus 194,990 fractional parts, then reappears in the west at dusk, ahead of the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行一度九十一分之二十一，九十一日行百一十二度而更順。

translations.literal: Prograde, swift: daily motion one degree and twenty-one parts in ninety-one; in ninety-one days it moves one hundred twelve degrees, then again prograde.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde and swift: one degree plus twenty-one parts in ninety-one per day, one hundred twelve degrees in ninety-one days, then slower prograde.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行一度十四分，九十一日行百五度而順。

translations.literal: Slow: daily motion one degree and fourteen parts; in ninety-one days it moves one hundred five degrees, then prograde.
translations.idiomatic: Slow: one degree plus fourteen parts per day, one hundred five degrees in ninety-one days, still prograde.

sentences.zh: 益遲，日行四十五分之三十三，四十五日行三十三度而留。

translations.literal: Increasingly slow: daily motion thirty-three parts in forty-five; in forty-five days it moves thirty-three degrees and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Still slower: thirty-three parts in forty-five per day, thirty-three degrees in forty-five days, then it stops.

translations.literal: Stationary, seven days, then turns back.
translations.idiomatic: Motionless for seven days, then it reverses.

sentences.zh: 逆，日行五分之三，十日退六度，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Retrograde: daily motion three parts in five; in ten days it retreats six degrees; ahead of the sun, it hides in the west at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde: three parts in five per day, six degrees back in ten days; ahead of the sun, it sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 逆，六日，退四度，而與日合。

translations.literal: Retrograde, six days, retreating four degrees, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde for six days, four degrees back, then it conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 凡再合一終，五百八十四日三十八萬九千九百八十分，行星如之。

translations.literal: In all two conjunctions one cycle: five hundred eighty-four days and three hundred eighty-nine thousand nine hundred eighty fractional parts; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Two conjunctions complete one cycle: 584 days plus 389,980 fractional parts; planetary travel the same.

sentences.zh: 水：晨與日合，伏，十一日退七度，而晨見東方，在日後。

translations.literal: Water: at dawn conjoined with the sun, it hides; eleven days retreating seven degrees, then at dawn appears in the east, behind the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury: conjoined with the sun at dawn, it disappears; after eleven days retreating seven degrees it reappears in the east at dawn, behind the sun.

translations.literal: Retrograde, swift: one day retreating one degree, then halts.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde and swift: one degree back in one day, then it stops.

translations.literal: Stationary, one day, then turns back.
translations.idiomatic: Motionless for one day, then it reverses.

sentences.zh: 順，遲，日行八分之七，八日行七度而順。

translations.literal: Prograde, slow: daily motion seven parts in eight; in eight days it moves seven degrees, then prograde.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde and slow: seven parts in eight per day, seven degrees in eight days, then faster prograde.

sentences.zh: 疾，日行一度十八分之四，十八日行二十二度，在日後，晨伏東方。

translations.literal: Swift: daily motion one degree and four parts in eighteen; in eighteen days it moves twenty-two degrees; behind the sun, it hides in the east at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Swift: one degree plus four parts in eighteen per day, twenty-two degrees in eighteen days; behind the sun, it vanishes in the east at dawn.

sentences.zh: 順，十八日二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分，行星三十六度二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分，而與日合。

translations.literal: Prograde, eighteen days and twenty million three hundred forty-four thousand two hundred sixty-one fractional parts, traversing thirty-six degrees and twenty million three hundred forty-four thousand two hundred sixty-one fractional parts, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde for eighteen days plus 20,344,261 fractional parts and thirty-six degrees plus 20,344,261 fractional parts, then it conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 凡一合，五十七日二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分，行星如之。

translations.literal: One conjunction: fifty-seven days and twenty million three hundred forty-four thousand two hundred sixty-one fractional parts; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: One conjunction: 57 days plus 20,344,261 fractional parts; planetary travel the same.

sentences.zh: 水：夕與日合，伏，十八日二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分，行星三十六度二千三十四萬四千二百六十一分，而夕見西方，在日前。

translations.literal: Water: at dusk conjoined with the sun, it hides; eighteen days and twenty million three hundred forty-four thousand two hundred sixty-one fractional parts, traversing thirty-six degrees and twenty million three hundred forty-four thousand two hundred sixty-one fractional parts, then at dusk appears in the west, ahead of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury: conjoined with the sun at dusk, it disappears; after eighteen days plus 20,344,261 fractional parts and thirty-six degrees plus 20,344,261 fractional parts it reappears in the west at dusk, ahead of the sun.

sentences.zh: 順，疾，日行一度十八分之四，十八日行二十二度而更順。

translations.literal: Prograde, swift: daily motion one degree and four parts in eighteen; in eighteen days it moves twenty-two degrees, then again prograde.
translations.idiomatic: Prograde and swift: one degree plus four parts in eighteen per day, twenty-two degrees in eighteen days, then slower prograde.

sentences.zh: 遲，日行八分之七，八日行七度而留。

translations.literal: Slow: daily motion seven parts in eight; in eight days it moves seven degrees and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Slow: seven parts in eight per day, seven degrees in eight days, then it stops.

translations.literal: Stationary, one day, then turns back.
translations.idiomatic: Motionless for one day, then it reverses.

sentences.zh: 逆，一日退一度，在日前，夕伏西方。

translations.literal: Retrograde, one day retreating one degree; ahead of the sun, it hides in the west at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde: one degree back in one day; ahead of the sun, it sets in the west at dusk.

sentences.zh: 逆，十一日退七度，而與日合。

translations.literal: Retrograde, eleven days, retreating seven degrees, then conjoins with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde for eleven days, seven degrees back, then it conjoins with the sun.

sentences.zh: 凡再合一終，百一十五日千八百九十六萬一千三百九十五分，行星如之。

translations.literal: In all two conjunctions one cycle: one hundred fifteen days and eighteen million nine hundred sixty-one thousand three hundred ninety-five fractional parts; planetary motion likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Two conjunctions complete one cycle: 115 days plus 18,961,395 fractional parts; planetary travel the same.

sentences.zh: 五星曆步術：以法伏日度餘，加星合日度餘，餘滿日度法得一從全，命之如前，得星見日及度餘也。

translations.literal: Five-star calendar step method: add the star-conjunction day-degree remainder to the hidden-day degree remainder by the prescribed divisor; when the remainder fills the day-degree divisor obtain one and carry from the whole; count as before to obtain the star's appearance day and degree remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Five-star step procedure: add the tabulated hidden-day and conjunction degree remainders; carry a whole unit when the sum fills the day-degree divisor, then index as before for the star's appearance day and fractional degree.

sentences.zh: 以星行分母乘見度分，如日度法得一，分不盡，半法以上，亦得一，而日加所行分，分滿其母得一度。

translations.literal: Multiply the appearance degree fraction by the star-motion denominator; divide by the day-degree divisor to obtain one; when the fraction does not exhaust, if it is half the divisor or more, also obtain one; then daily add the motion fraction, and when the fraction fills its denominator obtain one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply the appearance degree fraction by the motion denominator, divide by the day-degree divisor rounding up at half, then add the daily motion fraction until a full degree is reached.

sentences.zh: 逆順母不同，以當行之母乘故分，如故母而一，當行分也。

translations.literal: Retrograde and prograde denominators differ; multiply the old fraction by the current denominator and divide by the old denominator as one—this is the fraction for the current motion.
translations.idiomatic: When retrograde and prograde use different denominators, convert the prior fraction by the ratio of denominators to obtain the motion fraction for the current phase.

sentences.zh: 留者承前，逆則減之，伏不書度，除斗分，[55]以行母為率。

translations.literal: For stationary phases continue the prior value; for retrograde subtract; hidden phases record no degree; remove dipper fraction; [55] take the motion denominator as the rate.
translations.idiomatic: Stationary phases carry forward the prior value, retrograde phases subtract, hidden phases omit degrees, dipper fractions are cleared; per note [55], use the motion denominator as the rate.

translations.literal: When fractions have increase or decrease, the prior and following phases mutually govern one another.
translations.idiomatic: When fractional parts increase or decrease, successive phases adjust one against the other.

sentences.zh: 凡五星行天，遲疾留逆，雖大率有常，至犯守逆順，難以術推。

translations.literal: In general, as the five planets move through Heaven, their slow, swift, stationary, and retrograde phases follow a broad regularity; yet when they trespass, hold station, or reverse, it is hard to push by formula alone.
translations.idiomatic: Though the five planets generally follow broad patterns of slow, swift, stationary, and retrograde motion, their trespasses, halts, and reversals cannot always be forced by computation alone.

sentences.zh: 月之行天，猶有遲疾，況五星乎。

translations.literal: Even the moon's course through Heaven has slow and swift phases—how much more so the five planets.
translations.idiomatic: If even the moon shows slow and fast intervals in its course, the five planets do so all the more.

sentences.zh: 唯日之行天有常，進退有率，不遲不疾，不外不內，人君德也。

translations.literal: Only the sun's course through Heaven is constant; advance and retreat follow a fixed rate—neither slow nor swift, neither outward nor inward. Such is the virtue of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Only the sun moves through Heaven at a fixed pace, advancing and retreating by a steady rate—neither lagging nor rushing, neither straying outward nor inward. That is the virtue of the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 求木合終歲數法，以木日度法乘一木終之日，內分，周天除之，即得也。

translations.literal: Method for seeking Wood's total cycle year-count: multiply Wood's day-degree divisor by the days of one Wood cycle including fractional parts; divide by the circuit of heaven—this is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: To derive Jupiter's total cycle year-count, multiply its day-degree divisor by one complete cycle in days and fractional parts, then divide by the circuit of heaven.

sentences.zh: 求木合終合數法，以木日度法乘周天，滿紀法，所得復以周天除之，即得。

translations.literal: Method for seeking Wood's total cycle conjunction-count: multiply Wood's day-degree divisor by the circuit of heaven; when it fills the era divisor, take the result and again divide by the circuit of heaven—this is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: For Jupiter's total cycle conjunction-count, multiply the day-degree divisor by the circuit of heaven, reduce by the era divisor, then divide again by the circuit of heaven.

translations.literal: The five stars all follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The same method applies to all five planets.

sentences.zh: 魏黃初元年十一月小，己卯蔀首，己亥歲，十一月己卯朔旦冬至，臣偉上。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Wei's Huangchu era, the eleventh month was short; the obscuration head was Jimao; the year was Jihai; on the eleventh month, day Jimao, new moon, and winter solstice, subject Wei submitted this memorial."
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 1 of Wei, the eleventh month was short; the obscuration commenced on Jimao in a Jihai year; on the eleventh month, Jimao day, at new moon and winter solstice, Wei submitted this memorial."

sentences.zh: 劉氏在蜀，不見改曆，當是仍用漢四分法。

translations.literal: The Liu house in Shu saw no calendar reform; presumably they continued to use the Han Quarter-Remainder method.
translations.idiomatic: Shu under the Liu clan never adopted a new calendar and presumably kept the Han Quarter-Remainder system.

sentences.zh: 吳中書令闞澤受劉洪乾象法於東萊徐岳字公河。

translations.literal: Kan Ze, Director of the Secretariat in Wu, received Liu Hong's Supernal Icon method from Xu Yue of Donglai, styled Gonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ze, Director of the Secretariat in Wu, learned Liu Hong's Supernal Icon calendar from Xu Yue of Donglai, known as Gonghe.

sentences.zh: 故孫氏用乾象曆，至于吳亡。

translations.literal: Therefore the Sun house used the Supernal Icon calendar until Wu's fall.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun regime therefore employed the Supernal Icon calendar until Wu fell.

sentences.zh: 史臣按鄒衍五德，周為火行。

translations.literal: The historiographer notes that in Zou Yan's Five Phases, Zhou was the Fire phase.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer observes that in Zou Yan's scheme of the Five Phases, Zhou belonged to Fire.

sentences.zh: 衍生在周時，不容不知周氏行運。

translations.literal: Zou Yan lived in Zhou times; he cannot have been ignorant of Zhou's phase and cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yan lived during the Zhou age; he can hardly have been unaware of Zhou's assigned phase.

sentences.zh: 且周之為曆年八百，秦氏即有周之建國也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhou's calendar spanned eight hundred years, and the Qin house already possessed Zhou's founding date.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Zhou calendar ran eight hundred years, and the Qin house already held the record of Zhou's founding.

translations.literal: Zhou's Fire and Wood phases are easily verified in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The question of Zhou as Fire or Wood is easily settled on the evidence.

sentences.zh: 且五德更王，唯有二家之說。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the succession of the Five Phases through dynastic change, only two schools of explanation exist.
translations.idiomatic: On the rotation of dynastic phases, only two major schools of interpretation exist.

sentences.zh: 鄒衍以相勝立體，劉向以相生為義。

translations.literal: Zou Yan established his system on mutual conquest; Liu Xiang took mutual generation as the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yan built his theory on mutual conquest; Liu Xiang on mutual generation.

sentences.zh: 據以為言，不得出此二家者。

translations.literal: Judging by these statements, the argument cannot go outside these two schools.
translations.idiomatic: On these grounds, no serious account can escape one of the two schools.

sentences.zh: 假使即劉向之說，周為木行，秦氏代周，改其行運。

translations.literal: Suppose one follows Liu Xiang's view that Zhou was the Wood phase and the Qin house replaced Zhou and changed its phase-cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose one accepts Liu Xiang's claim that Zhou was Wood and that Qin, replacing Zhou, altered the phase succession.

translations.literal: If not by mutual conquest, then what conquers Wood is Metal;
translations.idiomatic: On the conquest theory, Wood should yield to Metal;

translations.literal: on mutual generation, Wood truly generates Fire.
translations.idiomatic: on the generation theory, Wood ought to produce Fire.

sentences.zh: 秦氏乃稱水德，理非謬然。

translations.literal: Yet the Qin house called itself the Water phase—this reasoning is hardly absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qin proclaimed itself Water—a claim that fits neither scheme cleanly.

sentences.zh: 斯則劉氏所證為不值矣。

translations.literal: Then the proof offered by the Liu school is worthless.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's argument therefore fails to convince.

sentences.zh: 臣以為張蒼雖是漢臣，生與周接，司秦柱下，備覩圖書。

translations.literal: This subject considers that although Zhang Cang was a Han minister, he was born in contact with Zhou, served Qin as Keeper of the Pillars below, and saw the full store of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhang Cang was a Han official, he had lived into Zhou times, served Qin as Keeper of the Pillars below, and had access to the full archive.

sentences.zh: 且秦雖滅學，不廢術數，則有周遺文雖不畢在，據漢水行，事非虛作。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Qin abolished classical learning, it did not discard numerology and calendrics; Zhou documents, though not all preserved, still survive in part. On the evidence of Han as Water, the claim was no empty invention.
translations.idiomatic: Qin suppressed the classics but not calendrical science; enough Zhou material survived to show that Han's claim to Water was not fabricated from nothing.

translations.literal: Jia Yi quoted Qin as saying: "Han is the Earth phase.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi cites Qin as saying, "Han belongs to Earth.

translations.literal: " Presumably this means that Han replaced Qin.
translations.idiomatic: "—meaning that Han supplanted Qin.

translations.literal: Examining the two theories in detail, each has its own logic.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the two theories, examined closely, has its own internal logic.

sentences.zh: 張蒼則以漢水勝周火，廢秦不班五德。

translations.literal: Zhang Cang held that Han Water conquered Zhou Fire and therefore abolished Qin from the Five-Phase succession.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cang argued that Han Water conquered Zhou Fire and therefore excluded Qin from the phase sequence.

sentences.zh: 賈誼則以漢土勝秦水，以秦為一代。

translations.literal: Jia Yi held that Han Earth conquered Qin Water and treated Qin as a full dynasty in its own right.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi held that Han Earth conquered Qin Water and counted Qin as a legitimate dynasty.

sentences.zh: 論秦、漢雖殊，而周為火一也。

translations.literal: Although Qin and Han differ in this respect, both agree that Zhou was Fire.
translations.idiomatic: However they differ on Qin and Han, both agree that Zhou was Fire.

sentences.zh: 然則相勝之義，於事為長。

translations.literal: Then the doctrine of mutual conquest is the more convincing in practice.
translations.idiomatic: On balance, the conquest theory fits the historical record better.

sentences.zh: 若同蒼黜秦，則漢水、魏土、晉木、宋金；

translations.literal: If one follows Cang in demoting Qin, then Han is Water, Wei Earth, Jin Wood, and Song Metal;
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhang Cang and demoting Qin yields Han Water, Wei Earth, Jin Wood, and Song Metal;

sentences.zh: 若同賈誼取秦，則漢土、魏木、晉金、宋火也。

translations.literal: if one follows Jia Yi in retaining Qin, then Han is Earth, Wei Wood, Jin Metal, and Song Fire.
translations.idiomatic: following Jia Yi and retaining Qin yields Han Earth, Wei Wood, Jin Metal, and Song Fire.

sentences.zh: 難者云：「漢高斷蛇而神母夜哭，云赤帝子殺白帝子，然則漢非火而何？

translations.literal: An objector says: "When Emperor Gaozu of Han cut the serpent, the divine mother wept at night, saying the Red Emperor's son killed the White Emperor's son—then surely Han is not Fire but what?"
translations.idiomatic: One critic asks: "When Han Gaozu cut the serpent, the divine mother wept in the night that the Red Emperor's son had slain the White Emperor's son—does this not prove Han was Fire?"

translations.literal: " This too is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: That objection, too, misses the point.

sentences.zh: 漢若為火，則當云赤帝，不宜云赤帝子也。

translations.literal: If Han were Fire, it should have been called the Red Emperor, not the Red Emperor's son.
translations.idiomatic: If Han were truly Fire, the omen should have named the Red Emperor himself, not his son.

translations.literal: What meaning does the White Emperor's son have in any case?
translations.idiomatic: And what, in any case, is meant by the White Emperor's son?

sentences.zh: 蓋由漢是土德，土生乎火，秦是水德，水生乎金，斯則漢以土為赤帝子，秦以水德為白帝子也。

translations.literal: It is because Han was the Earth phase: Earth is born from Fire; Qin was the Water phase: Water is born from Metal. Thus Han, as Earth, was the Red Emperor's son, and Qin, as Water, was the White Emperor's son.
translations.idiomatic: The answer is that Han was Earth—Earth born of Fire—and Qin was Water—Water born of Metal. Han as Earth was therefore the Red Emperor's son, and Qin as Water the White Emperor's son.

sentences.zh: 難者又曰：「向云五德相勝，今復云土為赤帝子，何也？

translations.literal: The objector also says: "Xiang said the Five Phases mutually conquer; now you also say Earth is the Red Emperor's son—how can this be?"
translations.idiomatic: The critic adds: "Liu Xiang taught that the Five Phases mutually conquer; how then can Earth also be the Red Emperor's son?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「五行自有相勝之義，自有相生之義。

translations.literal: " The reply: "The Five Phases have their own logic of mutual conquest and their own logic of mutual generation.
translations.idiomatic: The reply is that the Five Phases admit both a logic of conquest and a logic of generation.

sentences.zh: 不得以相勝廢相生，相生廢相勝也。

translations.literal: One cannot discard generation because of conquest, nor discard conquest because of generation.
translations.idiomatic: Neither principle cancels the other.

translations.literal: In conquest, Earth conquers Water;
translations.idiomatic: In conquest, Earth overcomes Water;

sentences.zh: 相生者，土自火子，義豈相關。」

translations.literal: in generation, Earth is itself born of Fire—the two meanings are not related."
translations.idiomatic: in generation, Earth is born of Fire—the two relationships are simply different."

sentences.zh: 崔寔四民月令曰：祖者，道神。

translations.literal: Cui Shi's Monthly Ordinances for the Four Peoples says: "Zu is the spirit of the road."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi's Monthly Ordinances for the Four Peoples states: "Zu is the spirit of the road."

sentences.zh: 黃帝之子曰累祖，好遠遊，死道路，故祀以為道神。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor's son was named Leizu; fond of distant travel, he died on the road; therefore he is worshipped as the spirit of the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor's son Leizu loved distant journeys and died on the road; for that reason he is honored as the road spirit.

sentences.zh: 嵇含祖道賦序曰：[56]漢用丙午，魏用丁未，晉用孟月之酉。

translations.literal: Ji Han's Preface to the Fu on the Road Spirit says: [56] Han used Bingwu, Wei used Dingwei, and Jin used the you day of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han's Preface to the Fu on the Road Spirit records: [56] Han used Bingwu, Wei Dingwei, and Jin the you day of the first month.

translations.literal: Thus no one knows whence Zu arose.
translations.idiomatic: No one can say with certainty when the cult of Zu began.

sentences.zh: 說者云祈請道神，謂之祖有事於道者，君子行役，則列之於中路，喪者將遷，則稱名於階庭。

translations.literal: Some say one prays to the spirit of the road and calls this Zu; when a gentleman sets out on service he arrays the rite along the road; when the bereaved are about to move the coffin they invoke the name on the courtyard steps.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that travelers pray to the road spirit and call the rite Zu: a gentleman departing on duty sets out the offering along the route; a family about to move a coffin invokes the name on the courtyard steps.

sentences.zh: 或云，百代遠祖，名諡彫滅，墳塋不復存於銘表，游魂不得託於廟祧，故以初歲良辰，建華蓋，揚綵旌，將以招靈爽，庶眾祖之來憑云爾。

translations.literal: Others say that over a hundred generations the remote ancestors' names and posthumous titles have faded, tombs no longer appear on inscriptions, and wandering souls cannot lodge in the ancestral temple; therefore at the year's first fine day they raise a decorated canopy and bright banners to summon the spirits, that the multitude of ancestors may come and draw near.
translations.idiomatic: Others say that after many generations names and tombs are lost and spirits have no temple to receive them; at the year's first auspicious day people therefore raise decorated canopies and bright banners to summon the dead, that all the ancestors may draw near.

translations.literal: Editorial note 57.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 57.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝時，侍中平原劉智，[58]推三百年斗曆改憲，以為四分法三百年而減一日，以百五十為度法，三十七為斗分。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Jin's time, Palace Attendant Liu Zhi of Pingyuan [58] pushed a three-hundred-year Dipper calendar reform, holding that the Quarter-Remainder method loses one day every three hundred years, taking one hundred fifty as the degree divisor and thirty-seven as the dipper fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Jin, Palace Attendant Liu Zhi of Pingyuan [58] proposed a three-hundred-year Dipper-calendar reform, arguing that the Quarter-Remainder system drops one day every three centuries, with 150 as degree divisor and 37 as dipper fraction.

translations.literal: He adorned it with inflated claims to support his reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: He padded the proposal with flattering rhetoric to bolster his case.

sentences.zh: 江左中領軍琅邪王朔之以其上元歲在甲子，善其術，欲以九萬七千歲之甲子為開闢之始，何承天云「悼於立意」者也。

translations.literal: Wang Shuo, Central Commander of the Left in the lands east of the Yangzi, finding its upper origin in a jiazi year and liking the method, wished to make the jiazi year ninety-seven thousand years from creation the beginning of the age—this is what He Chengtian called "grieving over the premise."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuo, Central Commander of the Left in the Eastern Jin, admired the method because its upper origin fell in a jiazi year and wanted to treat a jiazi ninety-seven thousand years from creation as the world's beginning—what He Chengtian dismissed as a flawed foundation.

sentences.zh: 景初日中晷景，即用漢四分法，是以漸就乖差。

translations.literal: The noon shadow at Jingchu used the Han Quarter-Remainder method, and for that reason gradually fell out of alignment.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingchu calendar's noon shadow measurements relied on the Han Quarter-Remainder method and therefore drifted steadily out of true.

translations.literal: In pushing the five planets, it was extremely loose and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Its planetary calculations were especially coarse.

sentences.zh: 晉江左以來，更用乾象五星法以代之，猶有前却。

translations.literal: Since the Eastern Jin, the Supernal Icon five-planet method replaced it, yet still showed advance and lag.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Jin the Supernal Icon planetary method replaced it, yet still showed forward and backward error.

sentences.zh: 宋太祖頗好曆數，太子率更令何承天私撰新法。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song was quite fond of calendrical computation; the Crown Prince's Director of Standards He Chengtian privately drafted a new method.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song took a keen interest in calendrical science, and the Crown Prince's Director of Standards He Chengtian privately composed a new system.

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 20 he submitted a memorial stating:

translations.literal: Your subject's nature is dull and slothful, and in youth I understood little.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is dull by nature and understood little in his youth.

sentences.zh: 自昔幼年，頗好曆數，耽情注意，迄于白首。

translations.literal: From childhood I have been fond of calendrical computation, giving my whole attention to it until white-haired old age.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood I have loved calendrical work and have pursued it with single-minded devotion into old age.

sentences.zh: 臣亡舅故祕書監徐廣，素善其事，有既往七曜曆，每記其得失。

translations.literal: My late maternal uncle, the former Director of the Secretariat Xu Guang, was skilled in these matters and kept a running record of the seven luminaries calendar, noting each success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: My late uncle, former Director of the Secretariat Xu Guang, was expert in these matters and kept a running ledger of the seven-luminaries calendar, noting every hit and miss.

sentences.zh: 自太和至太元之末，四十許年。

translations.literal: From Taihe through the end of Taiyuan was some forty years.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taihe era to the end of Taiyuan spans roughly forty years.

sentences.zh: 臣因比歲考校，至今又四十載。

translations.literal: Your subject has examined and corrected this over recent years; to the present is another forty years.
translations.idiomatic: I have tested and corrected that record in recent years, adding another forty years to the present.

sentences.zh: 故其疏密差會，皆可知也。

translations.literal: Thus its gaps, closeness, and convergences can all be known.
translations.idiomatic: Its errors and accuracies can therefore be known in detail.

sentences.zh: 夫圓極常動，七曜運行，離合去來，雖有定勢，以新故相涉，自然有毫末之差，連日累歲，積微成著。

translations.literal: The celestial pole is in constant motion; the seven luminaries run their courses; conjunction, separation, advance, and retreat follow a fixed tendency, yet as old and new phases interact, minute discrepancies naturally arise; day after day and year after year, tiny errors accumulate into visible ones.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's pivot turns without rest and the seven luminaries run appointed courses; though their meetings and partings follow broad regularities, the interplay of old and new cycles produces tiny discrepancies that, day by day and year by year, accumulate into plain error.

sentences.zh: 是以虞書著欽若之典，周易明治曆之訓，言當順天以求合，非為合以驗天也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents of Yu sets forth the canon of reverent accord, and the Changes illuminates the instruction to regulate the calendar—meaning that one should follow Heaven to seek agreement, not force Heaven to fit one's agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Yu Documents teaches reverent accord with Heaven, and the Changes instructs us to regulate the calendar—meaning that the calendar should follow Heaven, not force Heaven to follow the calendar.

sentences.zh: 漢代雜候清臺，以昏明中星，課日所在，雖不可見，月盈則蝕，必當其衝，以月推日，則躔次可知焉。

translations.literal: The Han dynasty mixed observations at the Clear Terrace, using stars at dusk, dawn, and culmination to test the sun's position; though the sun itself could not be seen, when the moon waxes full it must eclipse at opposition; by the moon one can infer the sun, and its lodge can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Han observers mixed measurements at the Clear Terrace, using dusk, dawn, and meridian stars to test the sun's place; though the sun itself is invisible, a full moon must eclipse at opposition, and from the moon one can infer the sun's lodge.

sentences.zh: 捨易而不為，役心於難事，此臣所不解也。

translations.literal: To abandon what is easy and labor the mind over what is difficult—this your subject cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: To leave the easy path and exhaust oneself over the difficult—this your subject cannot fathom.

sentences.zh: 堯典云「日永星火，以正仲夏」。

translations.literal: The Canon of Yao says, "The day is longest and the star is Fire—use this to fix midsummer."
translations.idiomatic: The Canon of Yao says, "The day is longest and the star is Fire—thereby fix midsummer."

translations.literal: Now at the last month of summer, Fire is on the meridian.
translations.idiomatic: Today, at the last month of summer, Fire crosses the meridian.

translations.literal: Also, "At midnight the star is Emptiness—use this to mark mid-autumn."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "At midnight the star is Emptiness—thereby mark mid-autumn."

translations.literal: Now at the last month of autumn, Emptiness is on the meridian.
translations.idiomatic: Today, at the last month of autumn, Emptiness crosses the meridian.

sentences.zh: 爾來二千七百餘年，以中星檢之，所差二十七八度。

translations.literal: Over the more than twenty-seven hundred years since, testing by meridian stars, the discrepancy is twenty-seven or twenty-eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Across the twenty-seven centuries since, meridian-star tests show a drift of twenty-seven or twenty-eight degrees.

sentences.zh: 則堯令冬至，日在須女十度左右也。

translations.literal: Then in Yao's command, winter solstice had the sun at about ten degrees of Maiden.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Yao's ordinance, winter solstice would have placed the sun near ten degrees of Maiden.

sentences.zh: 漢之太初曆，冬至在牽牛初，後漢四分及魏景初法，同在斗二十一。

translations.literal: The Han Taichu calendar placed winter solstice at the start of Ox; the Later Han Quarter-Remainder and Wei Jingchu methods both placed it at twenty-one degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Taichu calendar placed winter solstice at the start of Ox; the Later Han Quarter-Remainder and Wei Jingchu systems both placed it at Dipper 21.

sentences.zh: 臣以月蝕檢之，則景初今之冬至，應在斗十七。

translations.literal: Your subject, testing by lunar eclipse, finds that Jingchu's winter solstice today should fall at Dipper 17.
translations.idiomatic: Testing by lunar eclipse, I find that Jingchu's winter solstice today should fall at Dipper 17.

sentences.zh: 又史官受詔，以土圭測景，考校二至，差三日有餘。

translations.literal: Also the historiographical officers, receiving an edict, measured shadows with the earth-standard and compared the two solstices; the discrepancy was more than three days.
translations.idiomatic: Historiographical officers, under edict, measured solstice shadows with the earth-standard and found a discrepancy of more than three days.

sentences.zh: 從來積歲及交州所上，檢其增減，亦相符驗。

translations.literal: Examining accumulated years and reports from Jiaozhou, the increases and decreases also match verification.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-checking accumulated years and reports from Jiaozhou confirms the same drift.

sentences.zh: 然則今之二至，非天之二至也。

translations.literal: Then today's two solstices are not Heaven's two solstices.
translations.idiomatic: Today's solstices are therefore not Heaven's true solstices.

sentences.zh: 天之南至，[59]日在斗十三四矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's southern extreme: [59] the sun is now at thirteen or fourteen degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's southern extreme: [59] the sun now stands at Dipper 13 or 14.

sentences.zh: 此則十九年七閏，數微多差。

translations.literal: This means that seven intercalations in nineteen years is slightly too many.
translations.idiomatic: This implies that the nineteen-year, seven-intercalation rule runs slightly high.

sentences.zh: 復改法易章，則用算滋繁，宜當隨時遷革，以取其合。

translations.literal: To change the method and alter the rule would make computation ever more cumbersome; one should reform in timely fashion to obtain agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Constantly rewriting rules only multiplies computation; the calendar should be revised when needed to recover agreement with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 案後漢志，春分日長，秋分日短，差過半刻。

translations.literal: According to the Later Han Treatise, at the spring equinox the day is long and at the autumn equinox the day is short, the difference exceeding half a quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han Treatise notes that the spring equinox day is longer and the autumn equinox day shorter, by more than half a quarter.

sentences.zh: 尋二分在二至之間，而有長短，因識春分近夏至，故長；

translations.literal: Seeking the two equinoxes between the two solstices, there is nonetheless length and shortness; one recognizes that the spring equinox lies nearer summer solstice, hence the longer day;
translations.idiomatic: Since the equinoxes fall between the solstices yet differ in length, one sees that the spring equinox lies nearer summer and therefore yields a longer day;

translations.literal: the autumn equinox lies nearer winter solstice, hence the shorter day.
translations.idiomatic: while the autumn equinox lies nearer winter and therefore yields a shorter one.

sentences.zh: 楊偉不悟，即用之，上曆表云：「自古及今，凡諸曆數，皆未能並己之妙。

translations.literal: Yang Wei did not understand this and simply used it; in his memorial on the superior calendar he said: "From antiquity to the present, every calendrical system has been unable to match its own excellence."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei failed to grasp this and applied the values anyway; his memorial on the superior calendar boasts, "From antiquity to the present no calendar has matched its own perfection."

translations.literal: " Why did he not understand this, and how could he say such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: Yet how could he fail to see the problem and still make such a claim?

sentences.zh: 是故臣更建元嘉曆，以六百八為一紀，半之為度法，七十五為室分，以建寅之月為歲首，雨水為氣初，以諸法閏餘一之歲為章首。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject has newly established the Yuanjia calendar, taking six hundred eight as one era, half of that as the degree divisor, seventy-five as the lodge fraction, making the month containing Establishment of Spring the year's head and Rain Water the first qi, and taking years whose intercalary remainder is one as era heads.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject therefore proposes the Yuanjia calendar: era length 608, degree divisor 304, lodge fraction 75, year beginning at the month of Establishment of Spring, first qi at Rain Water, and era heads in years whose intercalary remainder equals one.

translations.literal: Winter solstice falls on the third day, fifth watch, before the upper day.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice is placed at the third day, fifth watch, before the upper day.

translations.literal: The sun's position is shifted four degrees from the old value.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's position is moved four degrees from the old placement.

sentences.zh: 又月有遲疾，合朔月蝕，不在朔望，亦非曆意也。

translations.literal: Also the moon has slow and swift phases; syzygy and lunar eclipse do not fall on new and full moon—this too is not the calendar's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The moon, moreover, has slow and fast intervals; syzygy and eclipse need not fall exactly on new or full moon—another point the old methods mishandle.

sentences.zh: 故元嘉皆以盈縮定其小餘，以正朔望之日。

translations.literal: Therefore Yuanjia always uses surplus and deficit to fix the small remainder and thereby correct the day of new and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjia system therefore uses surplus-deficit correction on the small remainder to fix the days of new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下允迪聖哲，先天不違，劬勞庶政，寅亮鴻業，究淵思於往籍，探妙旨於未聞，窮神知化，罔不該覽。

translations.literal: Bow humbly: Your Majesty extends the sage's course, anticipates Heaven without transgression, toils over the myriad affairs of government, and brightens the great enterprise; you probe the profound intent of former records and seek subtle principles not yet heard, exhausting spirit and knowing transformation—nothing escapes your survey.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, extending the Way of the sages and anticipating Heaven without offense, labors over the realm's affairs and illuminates the great enterprise; probing former texts and seeking principles not yet understood, you exhaust spirit and comprehend change—nothing lies beyond your view.

sentences.zh: 是以愚臣欣遇盛明，効其管穴。

translations.literal: Therefore this foolish subject rejoices to meet such brilliance and offers the measure of a tube and the insight of a needle-hole.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject, meeting such enlightened times, offers what little a narrow tube or needle's eye can contribute.

sentences.zh: 伏願以臣所上元嘉法下史官考其疏密。

translations.literal: I bow and wish that the Yuanjia method I submit may be sent down to the historiographical officers to examine its gaps and closeness.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully ask that the Yuanjia method I submit be referred to the historiographical officers for examination of its accuracy.

sentences.zh: 若謬有可採，庶或補正闕謬，以備萬分。

translations.literal: If in error there is anything worth adopting, perhaps it may supplement and correct omissions and mistakes, to serve the myriad parts.
translations.idiomatic: If any part proves usable despite its flaws, it may yet help correct errors and fill gaps.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「何承天所陳，殊有理據。

translations.literal: Edict: "What He Chengtian has set forth is exceptionally well reasoned.
translations.idiomatic: Edict: "He Chengtian's presentation is exceptionally well founded.

translations.literal: It may be sent out for detailed review."
translations.idiomatic: Send it out for detailed review."

sentences.zh: 太史令錢樂之、兼丞嚴粲奏曰：

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Qian Lezhi and Assistant Director Yan Can memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Qian Lezhi and Assistant Director Yan Can submitted:

sentences.zh: 太子率更令領國子博士何承天表更改元嘉曆法，以月蝕檢今冬至日在斗十七，以土圭測影，知冬至已差三日。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's Director of Standards and Director of the Imperial Academy He Chengtian memorialized to change the Yuanjia calendar method; testing by lunar eclipse places today's winter solstice at Dipper 17, and measuring shadow with the earth-standard shows winter solstice already three days in error.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian, Crown Prince's Director of Standards and Director of the Imperial Academy, petitioned to revise the Yuanjia calendar; lunar-eclipse tests place today's winter solstice at Dipper 17, and earth-standard shadow measurements show winter solstice already three days off.

translations.literal: An edict ordered it sent out for examination and verification.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the proposal sent out for verification.

sentences.zh: 以元嘉十一年被勑，使考月蝕，土圭測影，檢署由來用偉景初法，冬至之日，日在斗二十一度少。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia we received orders to examine lunar eclipses and earth-standard shadow measurements; examining the Jingchu method then in use, on winter solstice the sun stood at a little more than twenty-one degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 11 we were ordered to test lunar eclipses and earth-standard shadows; under the Jingchu method then in use, winter solstice placed the sun slightly past Dipper 21.

sentences.zh: 檢十一年七月十六日望月蝕，加時在卯，到十五日四更二唱丑初始蝕，到四唱蝕既，在營室十五度末。

translations.literal: Examining the full-moon eclipse of the sixteenth day of the seventh month of the eleventh year, the appointed hour was mao; from the fifteenth day, at the start of the second watch of the fourth drum in the chou hour, the eclipse began; at the fourth drum it ended, in the last degree of Encampment 15.
translations.idiomatic: For the full-moon eclipse on day 16 of month 7, year 11, the appointed hour was mao; the eclipse began on the 15th at the start of the second watch, fourth chou drum, and ended at the fourth drum in the last degree of Encampment 15.

translations.literal: Under Jingchu, on that day the sun stood at three degrees of Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu placed the sun that day at Chariot 3.

sentences.zh: 以月蝕所衝考之，其日日應在翼十五度半。

translations.literal: Testing by the moon's opposition, the sun that day should have stood at fifteen and a half degrees of Wings.
translations.idiomatic: By opposition, the sun should have stood at Wings 15½.

sentences.zh: [60]又到十三年十二月十六日望月蝕，加時在酉，到亥初始食，到一更三唱蝕既，在鬼四度。

translations.literal: [60] Again, for the full-moon eclipse of the sixteenth day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth year, the appointed hour was you; the eclipse began at the start of the hai hour; at the first watch, third drum, it ended, in four degrees of Ghost.
translations.idiomatic: [60] Again, for the full-moon eclipse on day 16 of month 12, year 13, the appointed hour was you; the eclipse began at the start of hai and ended at the first watch, third drum, in Ghost 4.

translations.literal: Under Jingchu, on that day the sun stood at three degrees of Woman.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu placed the sun that day at Woman 3.

sentences.zh: 以衝考之，其日日應在牛六度半。

translations.literal: Testing by opposition, the sun that day should have stood at six and a half degrees of Ox.
translations.idiomatic: By opposition, the sun should have stood at Ox 6½.

sentences.zh: 又到十四年十二月十六日望月蝕，[61]加時在戌之半，到二更四唱亥末始蝕，到三更一唱食既，在井三十八度。

translations.literal: Again, for the full-moon eclipse of the sixteenth day of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year, [61] the appointed hour was half of xu; at the second watch, fourth drum, near the end of hai, the eclipse began; at the third watch, first drum, it ended, in thirty-eight degrees of Well.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for the full-moon eclipse on day 16 of month 12, year 14, [61] the appointed hour was mid-xu; the eclipse began at the second watch, fourth drum, near the end of hai, and ended at the third watch, first drum, in Well 38.

translations.literal: [62] Under Jingchu, on that day the sun stood at twenty-five degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: [62] Jingchu placed the sun that day at Dipper 25.

sentences.zh: 以衝考之，其日日應在斗二十二度半。

translations.literal: Testing by opposition, the sun that day should have stood at twenty-two and a half degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: By opposition, the sun should have stood at Dipper 22½.

sentences.zh: [63]到十五年五月十五日望月蝕，加時在戌，其日月始生而已，蝕光已生四分之一格，在斗十六度許。

translations.literal: [63] For the full-moon eclipse of the fifteenth day of the fifth month of the fifteenth year, the appointed hour was xu; the moon had only just risen when a quarter of the eclipse light had already appeared, in about sixteen degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: [63] For the full-moon eclipse on day 15 of month 5, year 15, the appointed hour was xu; the moon had barely risen when a quarter of the disk was already eclipsed, near Dipper 16.

sentences.zh: 景初其日日在井二十四。

translations.literal: Under Jingchu, on that day the sun stood at twenty-four degrees of Well.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu placed the sun that day at Well 24.

sentences.zh: 考取其衝，其日日應在井二十。

translations.literal: Testing by opposition, the sun that day should have stood at twenty degrees of Well.
translations.idiomatic: By opposition, the sun should have stood at Well 20.

sentences.zh: 又到十七年九月十六日望月蝕，加時在子之少，到十五日未二更一唱始蝕，到三唱蝕十五分之十二格，在昴一度半。

translations.literal: Again, for the full-moon eclipse of the sixteenth day of the ninth month of the seventeenth year, the appointed hour was a little past zi; on the fifteenth day, before the second watch, first drum, the eclipse began; at the third drum, twelve-fifteenths of the disk were eclipsed, in one and a half degrees of Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for the full-moon eclipse on day 16 of month 9, year 17, the appointed hour was just past zi; on the 15th, before the second watch, first drum, the eclipse began; at the third drum twelve-fifteenths of the disk was eclipsed in Hairy Head 1½.

translations.literal: Under Jingchu, on that day the sun stood at two degrees of Room.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu placed the sun that day at Room 2.

sentences.zh: 以衝考之，則其日日在氐十三度半。

translations.literal: Testing by opposition, the sun that day should have stood at thirteen and a half degrees of Base.
translations.idiomatic: By opposition, the sun should have stood at Base 13½.

sentences.zh: 凡此五蝕，以月衝一百八十二度半考之，冬至之日，日並不在斗二十一度少，並在斗十七度半間，悉如承天所上。

translations.literal: For all five eclipses, testing by the moon's opposition of one hundred eighty-two and a half degrees, on winter solstice the sun was not at a little more than twenty-one degrees of Dipper but all within seventeen and a half degrees of Dipper—exactly as He Chengtian submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Across all five eclipses, opposition at 182½ degrees shows winter solstice not at Jingchu's Dipper 21+ but consistently near Dipper 17½—exactly as He Chengtian claimed.

sentences.zh: 又去十一年起，以土圭測影。

translations.literal: Again, from the eleventh year onward, shadows were measured with the earth-standard.
translations.idiomatic: From year 11 onward we also measured shadows with the earth-standard.

sentences.zh: 其年景初法十一月七日冬至，前後陰不見影。

translations.literal: In that year, by the Jingchu method, winter solstice fell on the seventh day of the eleventh month; before and after, overcast skies showed no shadow.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jingchu placed winter solstice on month 11, day 7; clouds before and after hid the shadow.

sentences.zh: 到十二年十一月十八日冬至，其十五日影極長。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth day of the eleventh month of the twelfth year came winter solstice; on the fifteenth day the shadow was longest.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice of year 12 fell on month 11, day 18; the longest shadow came on day 15.

sentences.zh: 到十三年十一月二十九日冬至，其二十六日影極長。

sentences.zh: 尋校前後，以影極長為冬至，並差三日。

translations.literal: Comparing before and after, taking the longest shadow as winter solstice, the discrepancy is uniformly three days.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing all years, the longest shadow consistently precedes the computed winter solstice by three days.

sentences.zh: 以月蝕檢日所在，已差四度。

translations.literal: Testing the sun's position by lunar eclipse, it is already four degrees in error.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar-eclipse tests already show the sun four degrees off.

sentences.zh: 土圭測影，冬至又差三日。

translations.literal: Earth-standard shadow measurement shows winter solstice again three days in error.
translations.idiomatic: Earth-standard shadows show winter solstice three days off as well.

sentences.zh: 今之冬至，乃在斗十四間，又如承天所上。

translations.literal: Today's winter solstice falls between fourteen degrees of Dipper—again as He Chengtian submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Today's true winter solstice falls near Dipper 14—again matching He Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 又承天法，每月朔望及弦，皆定大小餘，於推交會時刻雖審，皆用盈縮，則月有頻三大、頻二小，比舊法殊為異。

translations.literal: Also in He Chengtian's method, for each month's new moon, full moon, and quarter moons the large and small remainders are fixed; though the instants of syzygy and eclipse are carefully determined, all use surplus-deficit, so the month frequently shows three long or two short months in succession—quite unlike the old method.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's method also fixes large and small remainders for every new moon, full moon, and quarter; though syzygy times are carefully computed, the surplus-deficit correction produces runs of three long or two short months—quite unlike the old system.

sentences.zh: 舊日蝕不唯在朔，亦有在晦及二日。

translations.literal: In the old method, solar eclipses occurred not only at new moon but also at last day of month and on the second day.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old method, solar eclipses occurred not only at new moon but also at month-end and on the second day.

sentences.zh: 公羊傳所謂「或失之前，或失之後」。

translations.literal: This subject considers that this one provision should remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that this one rule should remain unchanged.

translations.literal: Staff Master for Miscellaneous Cavalry Pi Yanzong also challenged He Chengtian: "If last and first days fix large and small remainders, and the era head falls in surplus, then one day is dropped and the last day of the old year should become the head of the new era."
translations.idiomatic: Pi Yanzong, Staff Master for Miscellaneous Cavalry, also challenged He Chengtian: "If new and full moons fix the remainders and the era head lands in surplus, one day is dropped and the old year's last day should become the new era head."

sentences.zh: 」承天乃改新法依舊術，不復每月定大小餘，如延宗所難，太史所上。

translations.literal: " He Chengtian therefore revised the new method to follow the old procedure, no longer fixing large and small remainders each month, as Yanzong challenged and the Grand Astrologer submitted.

translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized: "Calendar reform is a great state rite; since Han and Wei it has been revised again and again.

sentences.zh: 良由術無常是，取協當時。

translations.literal: Truly because no method is eternally correct, one adopts what fits the time.
translations.idiomatic: No method stays correct forever; one adopts what fits the age.

sentences.zh: 方今皇猷載暉，舊域光被，誠應綜覈晷度，以播維新。

translations.literal: Now the imperial plan shines forth and old territories are illumined; one should indeed verify the gnomon and degrees to proclaim renewal.

translations.literal: He Chengtian's calendrical method is suitable for adoption.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's calendar is fit for adoption.

sentences.zh: 大餘之餘為朔小餘 各本並脫「大餘」二字，據晉志補。

translations.literal: The remainder of the large remainder is the new-moon small remainder: all editions omit the two characters "大餘"; supplied according to the Jin Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: On the new-moon small remainder: all editions omit 大餘; supplied per the Jin Treatise.

sentences.zh: 餘以通法約之 「以」下，各本並衍「朔」字，據晉志刪。

translations.literal: Reduce the remainder by the communication divisor: below "以," all editions also have the superfluous character "朔"; deleted according to the Jin Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: On reducing by the communication divisor: all editions add superfluous 朔 below 以; deleted per the Jin Treatise.

sentences.zh: 為入月日餘 「日」下各本並脫「餘」字，今從局本補。

translations.literal: As the day entered in month remainder: all editions omit the character "餘" below "日"; now following the Bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: On day entered in month remainder: all editions omit 餘 below 日; now following the Bureau edition.

sentences.zh: 度餘百四十七萬二千八百六十九 各本脫去「六十九」三字，據局本及晉志補。

translations.idiomatic: Degree remainder 1,472,869: all editions omit 六十九; supplied per the Bureau edition and Jin Treatise.

sentences.zh: 日餘二千三十四萬四千二百六十一 各本「千」上脫「四」字，今補。

translations.literal: Day remainder twenty million three hundred forty-four thousand two hundred sixty-one: all editions omit the character "四" above "千"; now supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Day remainder 20,344,261: all editions omit 四 above 千; now supplied.

sentences.zh: 副以章閏乘之 依文義，「副」字疑衍。

translations.literal: Auxiliary, multiply by rule intercalations: by the sense of the text, the character "副" is probably superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: On "auxiliary, multiply by rule intercalations": 副 is probably superfluous.

sentences.zh: 小餘二千四百一十九 「二千」各本並作「一千」，據局本及晉志改。

translations.literal: Small remainder two thousand four hundred nineteen: all editions read "一千" for "二千"; changed according to the Bureau edition and Jin Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Small remainder 2,419: all editions read 一千 for 二千; changed per the Bureau edition and Jin Treatise.

sentences.zh: 求後入月日 按所求者為後合入月日，「後」下當有「合」字。

translations.literal: To seek the next day entered in month: what is sought is the next conjunction day entered in month; below "後" there should be the character "合."
translations.idiomatic: On seeking the next day entered in month: 合 should follow 後.

sentences.zh: 以入月日日餘加入月日及餘 按所加者為一合的入月日及餘，「加」下當有「合」字。

translations.literal: Add the day entered in month and day remainder to the day entered in month and remainder: what is added is one conjunction's day entered in month and remainder; below "加" there should be the character "合."
translations.idiomatic: On adding day entered in month and remainder: 合 should follow 加.

sentences.zh: 除斗分 按依義當作「經斗除斗分」。

translations.literal: Remove dipper fraction: by the sense it should read "passing the Dipper, remove dipper fraction."
translations.idiomatic: On removing dipper fraction: the text should read 經斗除斗分.

translations.literal: Ji Han's Preface to the Fu on the Road Spirit says: all editions read "合祖賦序曰"; changed according to Shen Tao's explanation.
translations.idiomatic: On Ji Han's Preface to the Fu on the Road Spirit: all editions read 合祖賦序曰; changed per Shen Tao.

sentences.zh: 沈濤銅熨斗齋隨筆云：「此乃初學記卷十三禮部嵇含祖道賦序文。

translations.idiomatic: Shen Tao's Random Notes from the Bronze Iron notes: "This is Ji Han's Preface to the Fu on the Road Spirit in Initial Learning Record 13, Ritual Section.

sentences.zh: 『合』乃『含』字之譌，傳寫又奪『嵇』字『道』字耳。」

translations.idiomatic: 「合」 corrupts 「含」, and 「嵇」 and 「道」 were lost in transmission."

sentences.zh: 其日日應在翼十五度半 各本並作「翼十五度半」。

translations.literal: The sun that day should have stood at fifteen and a half degrees of Wings: all editions read "Wings fifteen and a half degrees."
translations.idiomatic: On "the sun that day should have stood at Wings 15½": all editions read "Wings 15½" without 其日.

sentences.zh: 按蝕既在營室十五度末，以月衝一百八十二度考之，其日日應在「翼十六度半」。

translations.literal: Since the eclipse ended in the last degree of Encampment 15, testing by the moon's opposition of one hundred eighty-two degrees, the sun that day should have stood at "sixteen and a half degrees of Wings."
translations.idiomatic: Since the eclipse ended in Encampment 15, opposition at 182° places the sun at Wings 16½, not 15½.

sentences.zh: 又到十四年十二月十六日望月蝕 各本並作「十二月」。

translations.literal: Again, for the full-moon eclipse of the sixteenth day of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year: all editions read "twelfth month."
translations.idiomatic: On the full-moon eclipse of month 12, day 16, year 14: all editions read "twelfth month."

sentences.zh: 按元嘉十三年十二月望月蝕，至元嘉十四年十二月望，已超過一蝕年，不當有月蝕。

translations.literal: The full-moon eclipse of the twelfth month of Yuanjia 13 to the full moon of the twelfth month of Yuanjia 14 already exceeds one eclipse year; there should not be a lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanjia 13 month 12 full moon to Yuanjia 14 month 12 full moon exceeds one eclipse year; a lunar eclipse is impossible.

sentences.zh: 今推元嘉十四年十一月望月蝕應在「井二十六度」。

translations.literal: Reckoning now shows the Yuanjia 14 eleventh-month full-moon eclipse should fall at "twenty-six degrees of Well."
translations.idiomatic: Recalculation places the Yuanjia 14 month-11 full-moon eclipse at Well 26.

sentences.zh: 其日日應在斗二十二度半 各本並作「二十二度半」。

translations.literal: The sun that day should have stood at twenty-two and a half degrees of Dipper: all editions read "twenty-two and a half degrees."
translations.idiomatic: On "the sun that day should have stood at Dipper 22½": all editions omit 其日.

sentences.zh: 按以此處所述各月蝕檢日所在，與景初曆所推者實差三度半，今景初其日日在斗二十五，則實際應在斗二十一度半。

translations.literal: Testing the sun's position by the lunar eclipses described here against the Jingchu calendar's values shows an actual discrepancy of three and a half degrees; now Jingchu places the sun that day at twenty-five degrees of Dipper, so the actual position should be twenty-one and a half degrees of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Testing these eclipses against Jingchu shows a 3½° error; Jingchu places the sun at Dipper 25 that day, but the true position is Dipper 21½.

sentences.zh: 今推是月望月蝕在井二十六度，以衝考之，亦與此數相合。

translations.literal: Reckoning now shows the full-moon eclipse of that month at twenty-six degrees of Well; testing by opposition also matches this number.
translations.idiomatic: Recalculation places that month's full-moon eclipse at Well 26; opposition agrees.

translations.literal: Therefore it should read "twenty-one and a half degrees."
translations.idiomatic: The text should therefore read "21½ degrees."

sentences.zh: 其前後並陰不見 按依上下文例，「見」下應有「影」字。

translations.literal: Before and after, overcast skies showed none: following the pattern of the context above and below, below "見" there should be the character "影."
translations.idiomatic: On "overcast skies showed none": following parallel passages, 影 should follow 見.

sentences.zh: 二十一日影極長 各本並作「二十一日」。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day the shadow was longest: all editions read "twenty-first day."
translations.idiomatic: On "twenty-first day the shadow was longest": all editions read only "twenty-first day."

sentences.zh: 按上下各例，以土圭測影，冬至各差三日，二十五日冬至，則應「二十二日影極長」。

translations.literal: Following the examples above and below, measuring shadow with the earth-standard, winter solstice in each case differs by three days; with winter solstice on the twenty-fifth day, the longest shadow should come on the "twenty-second day."
translations.idiomatic: Following parallel cases, earth-standard shadows place the longest shadow three days before computed winter solstice; with solstice on day 25, the longest shadow should fall on day 22.
